greek: Ὁ μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας λόγος ἐστὶν ἐλεύθερός τε καὶ αὐτεξούσιος, ὑπὸ μηδεμίαν βάσανον ἐλέγχου θέλων πίπτειν μηδὲ τὴν παρὰ τοῖς ἀκούουσι δι' ἀποδείξεως ἐξέτασιν ὑπομένειν. Τὸ γὰρ εὐγενὲς αὐτοῦ καὶ πεποιθὸς αὐτῷ τῷ πέμψαντι πιστεύεσθαι θέλει. Λόγος δὲ ἀληθείας ἀπὸ θεοῦ πέμπεται· διὸ καὶ τὸ ἐλεύθερον τὸ περὶ αὐτὸν οὐ φορτικόν. Κατ' ἐξουσίαν γὰρ φερόμενος εἰκότως οὐδὲ τὰς ἀποδείξεις τῶν λεγομένων ἀπαιτεῖσθαι θέλει, ὅτι μηδέ εἰσιν ἄλλαι παρὲξ αὐτῆς τῆς ἀληθείας, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ὁ θεός. Πᾶσα γὰρ ἀπόδειξις ἰσχυροτέρα καὶ πιστοτέρα τοῦ ἀποδεικνυμένου τυγχάνει, εἴ γε τὸ πρότερον ἀπιστούμενον, πρὶν ἢ τὴν ἀπόδειξιν ἐλθεῖν, ταύτης κομισθείσης ἔτυχε πίστεως, καὶ τοιοῦτον ἐφάνη ὁποῖον ἐλέγετο. Τῆς δὲ ἀληθείας ἰσχυρότερον οὐδὲν οὐδὲ πιστότερον, ὥστε ὁ περὶ ταύτης ἀπόδειξιν αἰτῶν ὅμοιός ἐστι τῷ τὰ φαινόμενα ταῖς αἰσθήσεσι λόγοις θέλοντι ἀποδείκνυσθαι διότι φαίνεται. Τῶν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ λόγου λαμβανομένων κριτήριόν ἐστιν ἡ αἴσθησις· αὐτῆς δὲ κριτήριον οὐκ ἔστι πλὴν αὐτῆς. Ὥσπερ οὖν τὰ διὰ τοῦ λόγου θηρώμενα, ἀπάγοντες ἐπὶ τὴν αἴσθησιν, ταύτῃ κρίνομεν, ὁποῖά ποτε ὄντα τυγχάνει, εἴτε ἀληθῆ εἴτε καὶ ψευδῆ, τὰ λεγόμενα, οὐκέτι δὲ κρίνομεν πιστεύοντες αὐτῇ, οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρωπίνους καὶ κοσμικοὺς λόγους ἀναπέμπομεν ἐπὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καὶ ταύτῃ κρίνομεν, εἴτε φαῦλοι εἴτε καὶ μὴ τυγχάνουσιν ὄντες, τοὺς δὲ τῆς ἀληθείας οὐδενὶ κρίνομεν ἑτέρῳ, πιστεύοντες αὐτῇ. Ἔστι δὲ ἀλήθεια ὁ θεός, ὁ πατὴρ τῶν ὅλων, ὅς ἐστι νοῦς τέλειος. Oὗ γενόμενος υἱὸς ὁ λόγος ἦλθεν εἰς ἡμᾶς, σάρκα φορέσας, ἑαυτόν τε καὶ τὸν πατέρα μηνύων, διδοὺς ἡμῖν ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν καὶ τὴν μετὰ ταῦτα ζωὴν αἰώνιον. Ἔστι δὲ οὗτος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν καὶ δεσπότης· οὗτος τοίνυν αὐτός ἐστιν ἑαυτοῦ τε καὶ τῶν ὅλων πίστις τε καὶ ἀπόδειξις. ∆ιόπερ οἱ τούτῳ κατακολουθοῦντες καὶ γνόντες αὐτόν, τὴν εἰς αὐτὸν πίστιν ὡς ἀπόδειξιν ἔχοντες, ἀναπαύονται ἐπ' αὐτῷ. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ πολλοὺς ὁ ἀντικείμενος πολεμῶν οὐ παύεται, πολλαῖς δὲ καὶ ποικίλαις μεθόδοις πρὸς ἐπιβουλὴν χρῆται, πρὸς μὲν τοὺς πεπιστευκότας, ἵνα τούτους τῆς πίστεως ἀπαγάγῃ, πρὸς δὲ τοὺς ἀπίστους ἔτι, ἵνα μὴ πιστεύσωσιν, ἀναγκαῖον εἶναί μοι δοκεῖ καὶ ἡμᾶς, καθωπλισμένους τοῖς τῆς πίστεως λόγοις ἀτρώτοις οὖσιν, ἀντιπολεμεῖν αὐτῷ διὰ τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Resurrection belongs to the fallen body; spirit does not fall. The soul dwells in the body, yet it does not live in what is soulless; when the soul departs, the body ceases to be. The body is the soul's house, and the soul is the spirit's house. These three — body, soul, and spirit — will be saved for those who hold pure hope and unwavering faith in God.

Even if we weigh the world's own arguments, we find nothing in them that makes the body's rebirth impossible. On top of that, the Savior demonstrates the salvation of our flesh throughout the entire Gospel. So why do we still tolerate unbelieving, scandalous talk? Why do we forget ourselves and turn back when we hear that the soul is immortal while the body is perishable and supposedly unable to rise again? We heard that very claim long before we learned the truth from Pythagoras and Plato. If the Savior merely taught those things and proclaimed the soul's life alone, what new gift did he bring beyond Pythagoras, Plato, and their circle? But he came announcing a new and strange hope to humanity. And it was indeed strange and new: God promises not to preserve immortality by means of immortality, but to turn corruption into immortality.

Unable to destroy the Word in any other way, the ruler of wickedness dispatched his own apostles, choosing them from the very ones who crucified our Savior. They bore the Savior's name, yet they did the works of the one who sent them, and through them blasphemy clung to that name. They introduced evil, pestilential teachings.

If the body does not rise, why do we still guard it? Why not simply let it serve its desires? Why not imitate those physicians who, once they have a patient they cannot save, allow him to indulge his appetites? They know he is perishing. That is exactly what those who hate the body do: they cast it out of the inheritance, as far as they can, and they dishonor it as though it were already dead.

But our physician, Jesus Christ, has pulled us away from desires and puts our body on the sober, self‑controlled regimen that belongs to him. It is clear, then, that he guards the body because it carries the hope of salvation from sins — just as physicians do not permit patients who have hope of recovery to serve their pleasures.

greek: Ἀνάστασίς ἐστι τοῦ πεπτωκότος σαρκίου· πνεῦμα γὰρ οὐ πίπτει. Ψυχὴ ἐν σώματί ἐστιν, οὐ ζῇ δὲ ἄψυχον· σῶμα, ψυχῆς ἀπολειπούσης, οὐκ ἔστιν. Oἶκος γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ψυχῆς, πνεύματος δὲ ψυχὴ οἶκος. Τὰ τρία δὲ ταῦτα τοῖς ἐλπίδα εἰλικρινῆ καὶ πίστιν ἀδιάκριτον ἐν τῷ θεῷ ἔχουσι σωθήσεται. Θεωροῦντες γοῦν καὶ τοὺς κοσμικοὺς λόγους, καὶ κατ' αὐτοὺς οὐχ εὑρίσκοντες ἀδύνατον ὑπάρχειν τῇ σαρκὶ τὴν παλιγγενεσίαν, καὶ ἐπὶ τούτοις πᾶσι τὸν σωτῆρα διὰ παντὸς τοῦ εὐαγγελίου δεικνύντα τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν, τί λοιπὸν ἀνεχόμεθα τῶν ἀπίστων καὶ σκανδάλων λόγων, καὶ λανθάνομεν ἑαυτοὺς ἐπιστρέφοντες εἰς τοὐπίσω, ὁπόταν ἀκούσωμεν ὅτι ἡ μὲν ψυχὴ ἀθάνατός ἐστι, τὸ δὲ σῶμα φθαρτὸν καὶ οὐκέτι δυνάμενον ἀναζῆσαι; Ταῦτα γὰρ καὶ πρὸ τοῦ μαθεῖν τὴν ἀλήθειαν παρὰ Πυθαγόρου καὶ Πλάτωνος ἠκούομεν. Eἰ οὖν ταῦτα ἔλεγεν ὁ σωτὴρ καὶ μόνης τῆς ψυχῆς τὴν ζωὴν εὐηγγελίζετο, τί καινὸν ἡμῖν ἔφερε παρὰ Πυθαγόραν καὶ Πλάτωνα καὶ τὸν τούτων χορόν; Νῦν δὲ τὴν καινὴν καὶ ξένην εὐαγγελιζόμενος ἦλθεν ἀνθρώποις ἐλπίδα. Ξένον δὲ ἄρα ἦν καὶ καινὸν τὸ τὸν θεὸν ὑπισχνεῖσθαι μὴ τῇ ἀφθαρσίᾳ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν τηρεῖν, ἀλλὰ τὴν φθορὰν ἀφθαρσίαν ποιεῖν. Ἀλλὰ γὰρ οὐκ ἄλλως λυμαίνεσθαι τὸν λόγον δυνάμενος ὁ τῆς πονηρίας ἄρχων ἐξέπεμψε τοὺς ἀποστόλους αὐτοῦ, κακὰς καὶ λοιμώδεις διδασκαλίας εἰσάγοντας, ἐκλεξάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῶν σταυρωσάντων τὸν σωτῆρα ἡμῶν, οἵτινες τὸ μὲν ὄνομα τοῦ σωτῆρος ἔφερον, τὰ δὲ ἔργα τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτοὺς ἐποίουν, δι' οὓς καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι ἠκολούθησεν ἡ βλασφημία. Eἰ δὲ μὴ ἀνίσταται ἡ σάρξ, διὰ τί καὶ φυλάσσεται καὶ οὐ μᾶλλον αὐτῇ συγχωροῦμεν χρήσασθαι ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις, καὶ οὐ μιμούμεθα τοὺς ἰατρούς, οἵτινες, ἐπειδὰν ἀπεγνωσμένον ἔχωσιν ἄνθρωπον σώζεσθαι μὴ δυνάμενον, ἐπιτρέπουσιν αὐτῷ ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις ὑπηρετεῖν; Ἴσασι γὰρ ὅτι ἀπόλλυται. Ὅπερ ἀμέλει ποιοῦσιν οἱ τὴν σάρκα μισοῦντες, ἐκβάλλοντες αὐτὴν τῆς κληρονομίας, τὸ ὅσον ἐπ' αὐτοῖς· διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ὡς νεκρὰν ἐσομένην ἀτιμάζουσιν αὐτήν. Eἰ δὲ ὁ ἡμέτερος ἰατρὸς Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστός, ἀπὸ τῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν ἡμῶν ἀποσπάσας, διαιτᾶται τῇ κατ' αὐτὸν σώφρονι καὶ ἐγκρατεῖ διαίτῃ τὴν σάρκα ἡμῶν, δῆλον ὡς ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας ἔχουσαν ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων αὐτὴν φυλάσσει, καθάπερ τοὺς ἐλπίδα σωτηρίας ἔχοντας ἀνθρώπους οἱ ἰατροὶ οὐκ ἐῶσιν ὑπηρετεῖν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Opponents deny that the flesh will rise. They argue it is impossible for this perishable, dissolving body to be reassembled into the same whole. They claim its salvation is both impossible and useless; they blame its frailties, parade its defects, and declare it the sole cause of sin, so that, if the flesh is to rise, they say, its weaknesses will rise with it. They construct sophistries like these: If the flesh rises, it will rise either whole, possessing all its members, or incomplete. But rising incomplete would reveal the raiser's weakness, if he could save some parts but not others. If it has all its parts and members, then it is clear that these things must exist after the resurrection from the dead — how is that not absurd, since the Savior said: "They neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven"? (Matthew 22:30) For angels, they say, have no flesh, do not eat, and do not cohabit; therefore there will be no fleshly resurrection. By saying these and similar things they try to turn people away from the faith.

Some even claim that Jesus himself is merely spiritual, no longer in flesh, and that he only provided an appearance of flesh, trying to deprive the flesh of the promise. First we will resolve the difficulties they raise; then we will advance the argument that demonstrates how the flesh possesses salvation.

greek: Φασὶν οἱ χείρονα λέγοντες οὐκ εἶναι τῆς σαρκὸς ἀνάστασιν. Ἀδύνατον γὰρ εἶναι τὴν φθειρομένην καὶ διαλυομένην ταύτην συναχθῆναι εἰς τὸ αὐτό. Πρὸς δὲ τὸ ἀδύνατον καὶ ἀσύμφορόν φασιν ὑπάρχειν τὴν ταύτης σωτηρίαν, καὶ κακίζουσιν αὐτὴν τὰ ἐλαττώματα προφέροντες, καὶ αὐτὴν μόνην τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων αἰτίαν ἀποφαίνονται, ὥστε, εἰ μέλλει, φασί, σὰρξ ἀνίστασθαι, καὶ τὰ ἐλαττώματα συναναστήσεται. Καὶ σοφίσματα πλέκουσι τοιαῦτα· Eἰ ἡ σὰρξ ἀνίσταται, ἤτοι ὁλόκληρος ἀναστήσεται καὶ πάντα τὰ μόρια ἔχουσα ἢ ἀτελής. Ἀλλὰ τὸ μὲν ἐλλειπῆ μέλλειν αὐτὴν ἀνίστασθαι ἀδυναμίαν ἐμφαίνει τοῦ ἀνιστῶντος, εἰ τὰ μὲν ἠδυνήθη σῶσαι, τὰ δὲ οὔ. Eἰ δὲ πάντα τὰ μέρη καὶ τὰ μόρια ἕξει, δῆλον ὅτι ταῦτα λέγειν ὑπάρχειν μετὰ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν πῶς οὐκ ἄτοπον, τοῦ σωτῆρος εἰρηκότος· Oὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίσκονται, ἀλλ' ἔσονται ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ; Oἱ δὲ ἄγγελοι, φασίν, οὔτε σάρκα ἔχουσιν οὔτε ἐσθίουσιν οὔτε συνουσιάζουσιν· ὥστε οὐδὲ σαρκικὴ ἀνάστασις γενήσεται. Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν καὶ τὰ τούτοις ὅμοια λέγοντες πειρῶνται διαστρέφειν τοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως. Eἰσὶ δέ τινες οἳ λέγουσι καὶ αὐτὸν τὸν Ἰησοῦν πνευματικὸν μόνον παρεῖναι, μηκέτι ἐν σαρκί, φαντασίαν δὲ σαρκὸς παρεσχηκέναι, πειρώμενοι καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀποστερεῖν τῆς ἐπαγγελίας τὴν σάρκα. Πρῶτον μὲν τὰ ὑπ' αὐτῶν δοκοῦντα ἄπορα φαίνεσθαι λύσομεν· εἶθ' οὕτως ἑξῆς ἐπάξομεν τὸν ἀποδεικνύντα λόγον περὶ τῆς σαρκὸς ὡς ἔχει σωτηρίαν.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Yes, they say. If the flesh rises, then it rises exactly as it was laid down—so that if it was laid down blind in one eye, it rises blind in one eye; if lame, it rises lame; if any other part of the body was lacking, the person rises still inferior because of that. How blind the true eyes of their hearts are! Did they not see on earth blind people recovering their sight and lame people walking by His word? The Savior did all these things, first so that what was spoken about Him through the prophets might be fulfilled—that the blind receive sight and the deaf hear, and the other things (Isaiah 35:5)—and also to give faith that in the resurrection the flesh will rise whole. For if on earth He healed the weaknesses of the flesh and made the body whole, how much more will He do this in the resurrection, so that the flesh also rises whole and complete. In this way the things they regard as impossible will be healed.

Eἰ οὖν ἡ σὰρξ ἀνίσταται, καὶ τοιαύτη ἀνίσταται ὁποία κλιθήσεται, ὥστε, εἰ μονόφθαλμος κλιθήσεται, μονόφθαλμος ἀνίσταται, εἰ χωλός, χωλός, εἰ ἄλλο τι τοῦ σώματος ὑστεροῦν εἴη, τοῦτο καὶ ἐλάττων ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἀναστήσεται. Τετυφλωμένοι ὡς ἀληθῶς τὰ τῆς καρδίας ὄμματα! Oὐ γὰρ εἶδον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τυφλοὺς ἀναβλέποντας, χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας τῷ ἐκείνου λόγῳ; Ἂ πάντα ἐποίησεν ὁ σωτήρ, πρῶτον μὲν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ·ηθὲν περὶ αὐτοῦ διὰ τῶν προφητῶν, ὅτι Τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσι καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν καὶ τὰ ἄλλα, ἔτι δὲ καὶ εἰς πίστιν τοῦ ὅτι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ἡ σὰρξ ὁλόκληρος ἀναστήσεται. Eἰ γὰρ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τὰς ἀσθενείας τῆς σαρκὸς ἰάσατο καὶ ὁλόκληρον ἐποίησε τὸ σῶμα, πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τοῦτο ποιήσει, ὥστε καὶ ἀκέραιον καὶ ὁλόκληρον ἀναστῆναι τὴν σάρκα. Τὰ μὲν οὖν παρ' αὐτῶν νομιζόμενα ἄπορα τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον ἰαθήσεται.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Some who deny the resurrection of the flesh say it is impossible for it to rise; others claim it is not fitting for God to raise it because of its worthlessness and contemptibility; and still others argue that it has neither beginning nor promise. I think we should first engage with those who say it is impossible for God to raise it, because they are ignorant: they claim by word to be faithful, yet by their deeds they prove themselves unfaithful and even more unfaithful than the faithless. All the nations have believed in idols and have been persuaded that all things are possible for them, just as Homer, their poet, declares: 'The gods can do all things, and easily' (he added 'easily'—that is, *eukherōs*—to display the greatness of the gods' power). Yet these deniers appear far more unfaithful than the pagans. For if the nations have believed of their idols, their gods—who have ears but do not hear, eyes but do not see—that they can do all things, even though those gods are demons, as Scripture says, 'The gods of the nations are demons' (Psalm 96:5), then how much more ought we, who possess the exceptional and true faith, to trust our God, since we have proofs? First, there is the creation of the first-formed man, who was made from earth by God; this alone is a sufficient demonstration of God's power. Moreover, by observing the generation that follows from one another, we can see and marvel even more: from a tiny drop of moist seed such a vast living being is shaped. And indeed, if this came to pass only by promise and were not visibly occurring, it would be more unbelievable than anything else; but the result makes it more credible. Besides, our Savior has shown us the outcomes of the resurrection, which we will discuss shortly. For now, we demonstrate that the resurrection of the flesh is possible, asking pardon from the children of truth if we also appeal to arguments that seem external and worldly: first, because nothing lies outside God, not even the world itself, for it is His creation; second, because we address these arguments to the faithless. If we were speaking to the faithful, it would be enough to answer that we have believed; but now we must proceed through demonstrations. The proofs already mentioned are sufficient to show that the resurrection of the flesh is possible; yet because they are extremely faithless, we will bring a more compelling argument—not from faith, since they lack it, but from their own unfaithfulness, their mother, I mean worldly reasoning. For if we prove to them from these very sources that the resurrection of the flesh is possible, they deserve great shame if they can follow neither the things of faith nor the things of the world.

greek: Ἔτι δὲ καὶ τῶν λεγόντων μὴ ἀνίστασθαι τὴν σάρκα οἱ μὲν ὡς ἀδύνατον ἀναστῆναι λέγουσιν, οἱ δὲ ὡς μὴ προσῆκον τῷ θεῷ τὸ ἀνιστάνειν αὐτὴν διὰ τὸ εὐτελὲς καὶ εὐκαταφρόνητον αὐτῆς, οἱ δὲ ὅτι τὴν ἀρχὴν οὐδὲ ἐπαγγελίαν ἔχειν. Πρῶτον οὖν δοκεῖ μέν μοι πρὸς τοὺς ἀδύνατον εἶναι λέγοντας τῷ θεῷ τὸ ταύτην ἀναστῆσαι διεξελθεῖν, ὅτι ἀγνοοῦσιν αὐτοὶ τῷ λόγῳ λέγοντες ἑαυτοὺς εἶναι πιστούς, καὶ διὰ τῶν ἔργων ἀποδεικνύντες ἀπίστους ἑαυτοὺς καὶ τῶν ἀπίστων ἀπιστοτέρους. Τῶν γὰρ ἐθνῶν ἁπάντων ἐπὶ τὰ εἴδωλα πεπιστευκότων καὶ πεπεισμένων ὅτι πάντα δυνατὰ τούτοις ἐστίν, ὡς καὶ Ὅμηρος, ὁ ποιητὴς αὐτῶν, φησίν· Θεοὶ δέ τε πάντα δύνανται Καὶ ·εῖα– (ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ ·εῖα προσέθηκεν, ὅπερ ἐστὶν εὐχερῶς, ἵνα τὴν μεγαλειότητα τῆς τῶν θεῶν δυνάμεως ἐμφάνῃ), πολὺ οὖν τούτων ἀπιστότεροι φαίνονται. Eἰ γὰρ τοῖς εἰδώλοις τὰ ἔθνη, τοῖς θεοῖς αὐτῶν, οἳ ὦτα ἔχουσι καὶ οὐκ ἀκούουσιν, ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχουσι καὶ οὐκ ὄψονται, τὸ πάντα δύνασθαι πεπιστεύκασι, δαιμονίοις οὖσι, καθὼς ἡ γραφὴ λέγει, ὅτι Oἱ θεοὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν δαιμόνια, πολὺ μᾶλλον ἡμεῖς, οἱ τὴν ἐξαίρετον καὶ ἀληθῆ πίστιν ἔχοντες, ὀφείλομεν τῷ θεῷ ἡμῶν πιστεύειν, ἔχοντες τεκμήρια· καὶ πρῶτον μὲν τὴν τοῦ πρωτοπλάστου γένεσιν, ὅτι ἐκ γῆς ὑπὸ θεοῦ γέγονεν· ἱκανὸν γὰρ τοῦτο δεῖγμα τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ δυνάμεως. Ἔτι δὲ καὶ τὴν μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξ ἀλλήλων γένεσιν κατανοοῦσιν ἔστιν ἰδεῖν, καὶ θαυμάσαι μειζόνως, ὅτι ἐξ ἐλαχίστης ·ανίδος ὑγροῦ τηλικοῦτον πλάσσεται ζῶον. Καίτοι γε εἰ ἐν ἐπαγγελίᾳ καὶ τοῦτο ἦν καὶ μὴ ἐφαίνετο γινόμενον, πολὺ τῶν ἄλλων ἦν ἀπιστότερον· ἀλλὰ γὰρ πιστότερον αὐτὸ ποιεῖ τὸ ἀποτέλεσμα. Ἀλλὰ μὴν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἡμῖν ἔδειξεν ὁ σωτὴρ ἀποτελέσματα, ἃ μετ' ὀλίγον ἐροῦμεν. Νῦν δὲ τὸ δυνατὴν εἶναι τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς ἀνάστασιν ἐπιδεικνύομεν, συγγνώμην αἰτούμενοι παρὰ τῶν τῆς ἀληθείας τέκνων, εἰ καὶ τῶν ἔξωθεν εἶναι δοκούντων καὶ κοσμικῶν λόγων ἁπτόμεθα· πρῶτον μὲν ὅτι οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔξωθεν τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐδὲ αὐτὸς ὁ κόσμος· ποίημα γάρ ἐστιν αὐτοῦ· δεύτερον ὅτι πρὸς ἀπίστους τούτους ποιούμεθα τοὺς λόγους. Eἰ γὰρ πρὸς πιστούς, αὐταρκὲς ἦν ἀποκρίνεσθαι τὸ ὅτι πεπιστεύκαμεν· νῦν δὲ διὰ ἀποδείξεων χωρεῖν ἀναγκαῖον. Ἱκανὰ μὲν οὖν καὶ τὰ προειρημένα τεκμήρια πρὸς τὸ δυνατὴν εἶναι δεικνύειν τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς ἀνάστασιν· ἀλλ', ἐπεὶ λίαν εἰσὶν ἄπιστοι, καὶ ἀναγκαστικώτερον ἐπάξομεν τὸν λόγον, οὐκ ἐκ τῆς πίστεως, ὅτι μὴ τυγχάνουσιν ὄντες αὐτῆς, ἀλλ' ἐκ τῆς ἀπιστίας, τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῶν, λέγω δὴ τῶν κοσμικῶν λόγων. Eἰ γὰρ ἐκ τούτων ἐπιδεικνύομεν αὐτοῖς δυνατὴν εἶναι τὴν τῆς σαρκὸς ἀνάστασιν, πολλῆς δήπουθεν αἰσχύνης εἰσὶν ἄξιοι, εἰ μήτε τοῖς τῆς πίστεως μήτε τοῖς τοῦ κόσμου ἀκολουθεῖν δύνανται.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: I have, in fact, already demonstrated sufficiently to the Gentiles that the resurrection of the body is possible. But if the resurrection of the body is not found impossible even in the judgment of unbelievers, how much more impossible must it be in the judgment of believers! Next, we must answer those who dishonor the body and assert that it is unworthy of the resurrection or of the heavenly citizenship. They argue that its substance is first of all earth, and that afterwards it has become full of all sin, so that it even compels the soul to sin along with it. These people appear to be ignorant of the whole work of God, of the original creation and formation of man, and of the things in the world for the sake of which he was made. For does the Word not say, 'Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness' (Genesis 1:26)? What kind of man does it clearly speak of? It clearly speaks of a fleshly man. For the Word says, 'And God took dust from the earth and formed man.' It is clear, therefore, that man was fleshly when he was formed in the image of God. Then how is it not absurd to claim that the flesh, formed by God in His own image, is dishonorable and worthy of nothing? That the flesh is a valuable possession with God is clear, first, from its having been formed by Him, if indeed even the image of the Creator and Artist becomes valuable; and it is also possible to learn this from the rest of creation. For that for the sake of which the other things were made is the most valuable of all to the One who made them.

Ἑξῆς δὲ λεκτέον πρὸς τοὺς ἀτιμάζοντας τὴν σάρκα καὶ φάσκοντας μὴ ἀξίαν εἶναι τῆς ἀναστάσεως μηδὲ τῆς ἐπουρανίου πολιτείας· ὅτι πρῶτον αὐτῆς ἐστιν ἡ οὐσία γῆ, μετέπειτα δὲ καὶ μεστὴ γέγονε πάσης ἁμαρτίας, ὥστε καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἀναγκάσαι συναμαρτάνειν. Ἐοίκασι δὲ οὗτοι τὴν ὅλην τοῦ θεοῦ πραγματείαν ἀγνοεῖν, καὶ τὴν ἐξ ἀρχῆς γένεσιν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πλάσιν, καὶ τὰ ἐν κόσμῳ ὧν ἕνεκα γέγονεν. Ἢ γὰρ οὔ φησιν ὁ λόγος· Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν; Ποῖον; Σαρκικὸν δῆλον ὅτι λέγει ἄνθρωπον. Φησὶ γὰρ ὁ λόγος· Καὶ ἔλαβεν ὁ θεὸς χοῦν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς καὶ ἔπλασε τὸν ἄνθρωπον. ∆ῆλον οὖν ὡς κατ' εἰκόνα θεοῦ πλασσόμενος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἦν σαρκικός. Eἶτα πῶς οὐκ ἄτοπον τὴν ὑπὸ θεοῦ σάρκα πλασθεῖσαν κατ' εἰκόνα τὴν ἑαυτοῦ φάσκειν ἄτιμον εἶναι καὶ οὐδενὸς ἀξίαν; Ὅτι δὲ τίμιον κτῆμα ἡ σὰρξ παρὰ θεῷ δῆλον πρῶτον μὲν ἐκ τοῦ πρὸς αὐτοῦ πεπλᾶσθαι, εἴ γε καὶ εἰκὼν τῷ πλάστῃ καὶ ζωγράφῳ τιμία γινομένη· καὶ ἐκ τῆς λοιπῆς δὲ κοσμοποιΐας μαθεῖν πάρεστιν· οὗ γὰρ ἕνεκεν γέγονε τὰ λοιπά, τοῦτο πάντων τῷ ποιήσαντι τιμιώτατον.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Yes, they say the flesh is sinful, and so it forces the soul to sin along with it; they accuse the flesh in vain, heaping the sins of both onto it alone. For how could the flesh sin by itself if it did not have the soul leading and urging it on? It is like a yoke of oxen unloosed from each other: neither can plow alone. In the same way, once soul and body are loosed from their union, neither can do anything by itself. But if the flesh alone is sinful, then the Savior came for its sake, just as he said: "I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance" (Matthew 9:13). Since the flesh has been shown to be precious and glorious to God beyond all his works, it will rightly be saved by him. We must answer those who claim that, even if the flesh is the noblest of God's works and precious to him, it does not therefore possess the promise of resurrection. How is it not absurd that, after such great deliberation and being honored above all else, the Creator would abandon it to non-existence? A craftsman or painter who wants their works to endure so they may be glorified through them will restore them when they decay; would God then abandon his own possession and creation as if it were nothing, letting it cease to be? We call that futile labor, like someone who builds a house only to tear it down, or ignores a ruined house when able to rebuild it; we would not accuse a human of doing such a thing in vain, so how much less God? But the incorruptible, all-encompassing Mind is not like this. Let the unbelievers praise such a notion, if that is what their unbelief leads them to! In fact, he has called the flesh to resurrection and promises it eternal life. For where he proclaims the gospel to save the human being, he proclaims it to the flesh as well. What is a human being, if not a rational living creature composed of soul and body? Is the soul by itself a human being? No, it is the soul of a human being. Is the body by itself called a human being? No, it is called the body of a human being. Since neither is a human being on its own, but the human being is the combination of both, and since God has called the human being to life and resurrection, he has called not a part but the whole, which is soul and body together. When both exist together in the same reality, how is it not absurd to save one and not the other? Since it has been demonstrated that the flesh can experience rebirth, what distinction justifies saving the soul but not the flesh? Are they making God out to be envious? But God is good and desires all to be saved. Indeed, both our soul and our flesh have heard his gospel and believed in Christ Jesus; both have been washed, and both have worked righteousness. Do they therefore portray God as ungrateful or unjust, if he wills to save one of two believers but not the other? They answer: yes, but the soul is incorruptible, being a part of God and his breath, and so he wished to save what is his own and akin to him; the flesh, however, is corruptible and not from him as the soul is. What grace is there in that? And what display of his power and goodness, if he only saves what is naturally saved and is already a part of him? The soul possessed salvation from him by its very nature, since it is his part, his breath; saving the soul is no great thing, for salvation is inherent to it precisely because it is his part. But there is no grace in saving what is one's own; that is simply saving oneself. The one who saves his own part through himself saves himself, lest that part ever be in need. That is not the mark of the good. No one calls a person good merely for showing favor to their children and descendants; even the wildest beasts do that, and they would even die for their offspring. But if someone shows the same favor to their slaves, they would rightly be called good. For this reason the Savior also taught us to love our enemies, since he asked: "What credit is that to you?" He showed us that a good work consists not in loving only those who come from us, but also those outside. And what he commanded us to do, he himself did long before.

greek: Ναί, φασίν· ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ σάρξ, ὥστε καὶ τὴν ψυχὴν ἀναγκάζειν συναμαρτάνειν αὐτῇ, μάτην κατηγοροῦντες αὐτῆς καὶ τὰ τῶν ἀμφοτέρων ἁμαρτήματα μόνῃ περιτιθέντες. Ποῦ γὰρ καθ' ἑαυτὴν ἁμαρτῆσαι ἡ σὰρξ δυνήσεται, ἐὰν μὴ τὴν ψυχὴν ἔχῃ προηγουμένην καὶ προκαλουμένην αὐτήν; Ὥσπερ γὰρ ζεῦγος βοῶν λυθέντων ἀπ' ἀλλήλων τοῦ ζυγοῦ τῶν βοῶν οὐδέτερος αὐτῶν κατ' ἰδίαν ἀροῦν δύναται, οὕτως οὐδὲ ψυχὴ καὶ σῶμα λυθέντα τῆς συζυγίας καθ' ἑαυτὰ ποιῆσαί τι δύνανται. Eἰ δὲ καὶ ἡ σὰρξ μόνη ἁμαρτωλός, μόνης ταύτης ἕνεκεν ἦλθεν ὁ σωτήρ, καθώς φησιν· Oὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν. Ἐπειδὴ οὖν τιμία παρὰ θεῷ καὶ ἔνδοξος παρὰ πάντα τὰ ποιήματα δέδεικται ἡ σάρξ, δικαίως ἂν ὑπ' αὐτοῦ σωθήσεται. Λεκτέον οὖν πρὸς τοὺς λέγοντας ὅτι, εἰ καὶ τὰ μάλιστα τοῦ θεοῦ ποίημα τυγχάνει οὖσα καὶ τιμία αὐτῷ παρὰ πάντα, οὐκ εὐθέως καὶ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἔχει. Καίτοι πῶς οὐκ ἄτοπον τὸ μετὰ τηλικαύτης βουλῆς γενόμενον καὶ παρὰ πάντα τὰ λοιπὰ τίμιον περιορᾶν τὸν ποιήσαντα εἰς τὸ μηκέτι εἶναι; Eἶτα ὁ μὲν πλάστης καὶ ζωγράφος, εἰ τὰς εἰκόνας, ἃς ἂν ποιήσωσι, διαμένειν ἐθέλουσιν, ἵνα δι' αὐτῶν δοξάζωνται, φθειρομένας αὐτὰς ἀνακαινοποιοῦσιν· ὁ δὲ θεὸς τὸ αὐτοῦ κτῆμα καὶ πλάσμα περιεῖδεν ἂν ὡς τὸ μὴ ὄν, μηκέτι δὲ καὶ εἰς τὸ εἶναι; Ματαιοπόνον ἀποκαλοῦμεν, ὥσπερ εἴ τις οἰκίαν οἰκοδομήσας ἔπειτα καταλύοι, ἢ καταλελυμένην περιορῴη, δυνάμενος ἀναστῆσαι· τὸν δὲ θεὸν οὐκ αἰτιασόμεθα, ὅτι μάτην ποιεῖ; Ἀλλ' οὐχ ὁ ἄφθαρτος τοιοῦτος, οὐκ ἄφρων ὁ τῶν ὅλων πέφυκε νοῦς. Eὐφημείτωσαν οἱ ἄπιστοι, εἰ τὸ μὴ πιστεύειν ἔχουσιν αὐτοί! Ἀλλὰ μὴν καὶ κέκληκεν αὐτὴν ἐπὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν καὶ ἐπαγγέλλεται τὴν αἰωνίαν ζωήν. Ἔνθα γὰρ τὸν ἄνθρωπον εὐαγγελίζεται σῶσαι, καὶ τῇ σαρκὶ εὐαγγελίζεται. Τί γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλ' ἢ τὸ ἐκ ψυχῆς καὶ σώματος συνεστὸς ζῶον λογικόν; Μὴ οὖν καθ' ἑαυτὴν ψυχὴ ἄνθρωπος; Oὔκ· ἀλλ' ἀνθρώπου ψυχή. Μὴ οὖν καλοῖτο σῶμα ἄνθρωπος; Oὔκ· ἀλλ' ἀνθρώπου σῶμα καλεῖται. Eἴπερ οὖν κατ' ἰδίαν μὲν τούτων οὐδέτερον ἄνθρωπός ἐστι, τὸ δὲ ἐκ τῆς ἀμφοτέρων συμπλοκῆς καλεῖται ἄνθρωπος, κέκληκε δὲ ὁ θεὸς εἰς ζωὴν καὶ ἀνάστασιν τὸν ἄνθρωπον, οὐ τὸ μέρος ἀλλὰ τὸ ὅλον κέκληκεν, ὅπερ ἐστὶ τὴν ψυχὴν καὶ τὸ σῶμα. Ἐπεὶ πῶς οὐκ ἄτοπον, ἀμφοτέρων ὄντων κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ, τὸ μὲν σώζειν, τὸ δὲ μή; Oὐκ ὄντος γὰρ ἀδυνάτου, καθάπερ δέδεικται, τὴν σάρκα ἔχειν τὴν παλιγγενεσίαν, τίς ἡ διάκρισις, ὥστε τὴν μὲν ψυχὴν σώζεσθαι, τὴν δὲ σάρκα μή; Ἢ φθονερὸν ποιοῦσι τὸν θεόν; Ἀλλὰ ἀγαθός ἐστι καὶ σώζεσθαι πάντας θέλει· καὶ δὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῦ κηρύγματος αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ μόνον ἤκουσεν ἡ ψυχὴ ἡμῶν καὶ σὺν αὐτῇ ἡ σάρξ, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν, ἀλλ' ἀμφότερα ἐλούσαντο καὶ ἀμφότερα τὴν δικαιοσύνην εἰργάσαντο. Ἀρ' οὖν ἀχάριστον ἢ ἄδικον ἀποφαίνουσι τὸν θεόν, εἰ τῶν ἀμφοτέρων πιστευόντων ἐπ' αὐτὸν τὴν μὲν σώζειν θέλει, τὴν δὲ οὔ; Ναί, φασίν· ἀλλ' ἡ μὲν ψυχή ἐστιν ἄφθαρτος, μέρος οὖσα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐμφύσημα, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὸ ἴδιον καὶ συγγενὲς ἠθέλησεν σῶσαι· ἡ δὲ σὰρξ φθαρτὴ καὶ οὐκ ἀπ' αὐτοῦ καθάπερ ἡ ψυχή. Eἶτα τίς αὐτῷ χάρις; Καὶ τίς ἐπίδειξις τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ, εἰ τὸ μὲν φύσει σωζόμενον καὶ μέρος ὑπάρχον αὐτοῦ σώζειν ἤμελλεν; Aὐτὸ γὰρ ἐξ ἑαυτοῦ εἶχε τὴν σωτηρίαν, ὥστε τὴν μὲν ψυχὴν σώζων οὐ μέγα ποιεῖ· τὸ γὰρ σώζεσθαι πάρεστιν αὐτῇ, ὅτι ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ μέρος, ἐμφύσημα αὐτοῦ οὖσα. Ἀλλ' οὐδὲ χάρις αὐτῷ τὸ ἴδιον σώζοντι· τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ἑαυτὸν σώζειν. Ὁ γὰρ τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ σώζων δι' ἑαυτοῦ ἑαυτὸν σώζει, μή ποτε ἐκεῖνο τὸ μέρος ἐνδεὲς γένηται. Oὐκ ἔστιν ἀγαθοῦ τὸ τοιοῦτον. Oὐδὲ γὰρ ἄνθρωπον ἀγαθόν τις ἐρεῖ τὸν τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐγγόνοις χαριζόμενόν τι. Τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ τὰ ἀγριώτατα τῶν θηρίων ποιοῦσι· κἂν ὑπεραποθανεῖν τῶν ἐκγόνων αὐτῶν δέῃ, ἑκοντὶ τοῦτο ὑπομένουσιν. Eἰ δέ τις τὰ αὐτὰ τοῖς δούλοις παράσχοι, δικαίως ἂν οὗτος λέγοιτο ἀγαθός. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὁ σωτὴρ ἐδίδαξεν ἡμᾶς ἀγαπᾶν τοὺς ἐχθρούς, ἐπεὶ τίς ὑμῖν χάρις; φησίν. Ὥστε δέδειχεν ἡμῖν ἀγαθὸν ἔργον εἶναι τὸ μὴ τοὺς ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεγονότας μόνον ἀγαπᾶν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς ἔξωθεν. Ἂ δὲ ἡμῖν παρήγγειλε πολὺ πρότερον αὐτὸς ἐποίει. ***

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: If Christ had no need of the flesh, why did he heal it? The strongest proof of all is that he raised the dead. To what end? Was it not to demonstrate the kind of resurrection that is to come? How, then, did he raise the dead—was it their souls or their bodies? Clearly, it was both. If the resurrection were only spiritual, he would have needed to show his own body lying in the tomb and his soul existing apart from it. Instead, he did not do this; he raised the body, confirming the promise of life within it. Why, then, did he raise the flesh that had suffered, if not to reveal the bodily resurrection? To confirm this, he appeared to disciples who, though they saw him, still doubted whether he had truly risen in the body. 'Do you not yet have faith?' he said. 'See that it is I myself.' He let them touch him and showed them the nail marks in his hands. After they examined him from every side and recognized that he was truly himself, still in the body, they asked him to eat with them so they could learn through this act that he had risen bodily. He ate honeycomb and fish. Having proved that the resurrection is truly of the flesh, and wishing also to show—as he said our dwelling is in heaven—that it is not impossible for flesh to ascend into heaven, he was taken up before their eyes while still in the flesh. Therefore, if anyone still demands demonstrative arguments about the resurrection after all that has been said, he differs in no way from the Sadducees; for the resurrection of the flesh is the power of God and transcends all reason, confirmed by faith and witnessed in works.

greek: Eἰ εἰς μηδὲν ἔχρῃζε τῆς σαρκός, τί καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτήν; Καί, τὸ πάντων ἰσχυρότατον, νεκροὺς ἀνέστησε. Τίνος ἕνεκεν; Oὐχ ἵνα δείξῃ τὴν ἀνάστασιν οἵα μέλλει γίνεσθαι; Πῶς οὖν τοὺς νεκροὺς ἀνέστησε; Πότερον τὰς ψυχὰς ἢ τὰ σώματα; Ἀλλὰ δῆλον ὅτι ἀμφότερα. Eἰ δὲ ἦν πνευματικὴ μόνη ἡ ἀνάστασις, ἐχρῆν ἀναστάντα αὐτὸν κατ' ἰδίαν μὲν δεῖξαι τὸ σῶμα κείμενον, κατ' ἰδίαν δὲ τὴν ψυχὴν ὑπάρχουσαν. Νῦν δὲ τοῦτο μὲν οὐκ ἐποίησεν, ἀνέστησε δὲ τὸ σῶμα, τῆς ζωῆς τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν ἐν αὐτῷ πιστούμενος. Τίνος οὖν ἕνεκεν τῇ σαρκὶ τῇ παθούσῃ ἀνέστη, εἰ μὴ ἵνα δείξῃ τὴν σαρκικὴν ἀνάστασιν; Καὶ τοῦτο βουλόμενος πιστοποιῆσαι, τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ μὴ πιστευόντων εἰ ἀληθῶς σώματι ἀνέστη, βλεπόντων αὐτῶν καὶ δισταζόντων, εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Oὔπω ἔχετε πίστιν; φησίν. Ἴδετε ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι. Καὶ ψηλαφᾶν αὐτὸν ἐπέτρεπεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τοὺς τύπους τῶν ἥλων ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν ἐπεδείκνυε. Καὶ πανταχόθεν αὐτὸν κατανοήσαντες, ὅτι αὐτός ἐστι καὶ ἐν τῷ σώματι, παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν φαγεῖν μετ' αὐτῶν, ἵνα καὶ διὰ τούτου βεβαίως μάθωσιν ὅτι ἀληθῶς σαρκικῶς ἀνέστη. Καὶ ἔφαγε κηρίον καὶ ἰχθύν. Καὶ οὕτως ἐπιδείξας αὐτοῖς ὅτι ἀληθῶς σαρκὸς ἀνάστασίς ἐστι, βουλόμενος ἐπιδεῖξαι καὶ τοῦτο (καθὼς εἴρηκεν ἐν οὐρανῷ τὴν κατοίκησιν ἡμῶν ὑπάρχειν) ὅτι οὐκ ἀδύνατον καὶ σαρκὶ εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνελθεῖν, ἀνελήφθη βλεπόντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ὡς ἦν ἐν τῇ σαρκί. Oὐκοῦν, εἴ τις ἀπαιτεῖ μετὰ πάντα τὰ προειρημένα λόγους ἀποδεικτικοὺς περὶ ἀναστάσεως, οὐδὲν τῶν Σαδδουκαίων διαφέρει· ἐπειδὴ ἡ ἀνάστασις τῆς σαρκὸς δύναμις θεοῦ ἐστι καὶ ὑπεράνω λόγου παντός, βεβαιουμένη μὲν πίστει, θεωρουμένη δὲ ἔργοις. ***

excerpts.author: Lactantius
english: Therefore they will not be reborn, since that cannot happen; rather, they will rise again and be clothed with bodies by God. They will remember their former life and all their deeds, and, placed in heavenly blessings, they will enjoy the joy of countless riches and give thanks to God present among them, because He has destroyed all evil and raised them to the kingdom and eternal life.

The philosophers, too, have attempted to speak of this resurrection, but as corruptly as the poets. Pythagoras argued that souls pass into new bodies, yet ineptly — claiming they move from humans into beasts and from beasts back into humans, and that he himself was once Euphorbus. Chrysippus fared better; Cicero says he upheld the Stoic school. In his books on providence, when discussing the world's renewal, he wrote: 'Since this is so, it is clear that nothing is impossible, and that after we die we shall again be restored, in some cycle of time, to the very state in which we now exist.'

But let us turn from human speculations to divine testimony. The Sibyl declares: 'The whole race of mortals is faithless. But when the judgment of the world and of mortals arrives — the judgment God Himself will execute, judging the ungodly and the godly together — then He will consign the ungodly to darkness in fire. But those who are godly will live again upon the earth, the Spirit of God having granted them both honor and life.'

If not only prophets but also seers, poets, and philosophers agree that a resurrection of the dead will come, let no one demand from us an explanation of how it can happen. For no account can be given of God's works. But if from the beginning God fashioned man in some unspeakable manner, let us believe that the One who made the new can also restore the old.

latin: Non igitur renascentur, quod fieri non potest, sed resurgent et a deo corporibus induentur et prioris uitae factorumque omnium memores erunt et in bonis caelestibus conlocati ac fruentes iucunditate innumerabilium copiarum praesenti deo gratias agent, quod malum omne deleuerit, quod eos ad regnum uitamque perpetuam suscitarit. qua de anastasi philosophi quoque dicere aliquid conati sunt tam corrupte quam poetae. nam Pythagoras transire animas in noua corpora disputauit, sed inepte, quod ex hominibus in pecudes et ex pecudibus in homines et se ipsum ex Euphorbo esse reparatum. meiius Chrysippus, quem Cicero ait fulcire porticum Stoicorum: qui in libris quos de prouidentia scripsit cum de innouatione mundi loqueretur, haec intulit: τούτου δέ οὕτως ἔχοντος δῆλον, ὡς οὐδὲν ἀδύνατον, καὶ ἡμᾶς μετά τὸ τελευτῆσαι πάλιν περιόδῳ τινὶ χρόνου εἰς τοῦτο ἐν ᾧ νῦν ἐσμεν ἀποκαταστῆναι σχῆμα. sed nos ab humanis ad diuina redeamus. Sibylla dicit haec: δύσπιστον γὰρ ἅπαν μερόπων γένος. ἀλλ᾽ ὅταν ἠδὴ κόσμου καὶ θνητῶν ἔλθῃ κρίσις, ἣν θεὸς αὐτὸς ποιήσει κρίνων ἀσεβεῖς θ᾽ ἅμα εὐσεβέας τε, καὶ τότε δυσσεβέας μὲν ἐπὶ ζόφον ἐν πυρὶ πέμψει. ὅσσοι δ᾽ εὐσεβέουσι, πάλιν ζήσουσ᾽ ἐπὶ γαίης, πνεῦμα θεοῦ δόντος τιμὴν ἅμα καὶ βίον αὐτοῖς. quodsi non modo prophetae, sed etiam uates et poetae et philosophi anastasim mortuorum futuram esse consentiunt, nemo quaerat a nobis quemadmodum fieri possit. nec enim diuinorum operum reddi potest ratio: sed si a principio deus hominem nescio quo inenarrabili modo instituit, credamus ab eodem restitui ueterem posse qui nouum fecit.

excerpts.author: Didache
english: Stay alert for the sake of your life. Do not let your lamps go out, and do not let your loins grow slack; instead, be ready. You do not know the hour when our Lord will come. Meet together often, seeking what benefits your souls, because the whole time of your faith will not help you if you are not made complete in the final season. In the last days false prophets and corrupters will multiply, the sheep will turn into wolves, and love will turn into hatred. As lawlessness increases, they will hate one another, persecute one another, and betray one another. Then the world‑deceiver will appear as the Son of God; he will perform signs and wonders, the earth will be handed over to him, and he will do lawless things that have never happened from eternity. Then humanity will enter the fiery trial, many will fall away and perish, but those who endure in their faith will be saved by Him, the Foundation. And then the signs of truth will appear: first, an outspreading in heaven; second, the sound of a trumpet; third, a resurrection of the dead — not of all, but as it was said: "The Lord will come, and all the saints with Him." Then the world will see the Lord coming on the clouds of heaven (Matthew 24:30).

greek: Γρηγορεῖτε ὑπὲρ τῆς ζωῆς ὑμῶν: οἱ λύχνοι ὑμῶν μὴ σβεσθήτωσαν, καὶ αἱ ὀσφύες ὑμῶν μὴ ἐκλυέσθωσαν, ἀλλὰ γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι: οὐ γὰρ οἴδατε τὴν ὤραν, ἐν ᾗ ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν ἔρχεται. πυκνῶς δὲ συναχθήσεσθε ζητοῦντες τὰ ἀνήκοντα ταῖς ψυχαῖς ὑμῶν: οὐ γὰρ ὠφελήσει ὑμᾶς ὁ πᾶς χρόνος τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν, ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τῷ ἐσχάτῳ καιρῷ τελειωθῆτε. ἐν γὰρ ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις πληθυνθήσονται οἱ ψευδοπροφῆται καὶ οἱ φθορεῖς, καὶ στραφήσονται τὰ πρόβατα εἰς λύκους, καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη στραφήσεται εἰς μῖσος. αὐξανούσης γὰρ τῆς ἀνομίας μισήσουσιν ἀλλήλους καὶ διώξουσι καὶ παραδώσουσι, καὶ τότε φανήσεται ὁ κοσμοπλανὴς ὡς υἱὸς θεοῦ, καὶ ποιήσει σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα, καὶ ἡ γῆ παραδοθήσεται εἰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ποιήσει ἀθέμιτα, ἅ οὐδέποτε γέγονεν ἐξ αἰῶνος. τότε ἥξει ἡ κτίσις τῶν ἀνθρώπων εἰς τὴν πύρωσιν τῆς δοκιμασίας, καὶ σκανδαλισθήσονται πολλοὶ καὶ ἀπολοῦνται, οἱ δὲ ὑπομείναντες ἐν τῇ πίστει αὐτῶν σωθήσονται ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ καταθέματος. καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὰ σημεῖα τῆς ἀληθείας: πρῶτον σημεῖον ἐκπετάσεως ἐν οὐρανῷ, εἶτα σημεῖον φωνῆς σάλπιγγος, καὶ τὸ τρίτον ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν. οὐ πάντων δέ, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐρρέθη: Ἥξει ὁ κύριος καὶ πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι μετ’ αὐτοῦ. τότε ὄψεται ὁ κόσμος τὸν κύριον ἐρχόμενον ἐπάνω τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Justin: And that you may learn that it was for the sins of your own nation, and for their idolatries and not because there was any necessity for such sacrifices , that they were likewise enjoined, listen to the manner in which He speaks of these by Amos, one of the twelve, saying: 'Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! To what end is this day of the Lord for you? It is darkness and not light, as when a man flees from the face of a lion, and a bear meets him; and he goes into his house, and leans his hands against the wall, and the serpent bites him. Shall not the day of the Lord be darkness and not light, even very dark, and no brightness in it?

I have hated , I have despised your feast-days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies: wherefore, though you offer Me your burnt-offerings and sacrifices , I will not accept them; neither will I regard the peace-offerings of your presence. Take away from Me the multitude of your songs and psalms; I will not hear your instruments. But let judgment be rolled down as water, and righteousness as an impassable torrent. Have you offered unto Me victims and sacrifices in the wilderness, O house of Israel ? Says the Lord. And have you taken up the tabernacle of Moloch , and the star of your god Raphan, the figures which you made for yourselves? And I will carry you away beyond Damascus, says the Lord, whose name is the Almighty God .

Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria : those who are named among the chiefs have plucked away the first-fruits of the nations: the house of Israel have entered for themselves. Pass all of you unto Calneh, and see; and from thence go unto Hamath the great, and go down thence to Gath of the strangers, the noblest of all these kingdoms, if their boundaries are greater than your boundaries.

You who come to the evil day, who are approaching, and who hold to false Sabbaths ; who lie on beds of ivory, and are at ease upon their couches; who eat the lambs out of the flock, and the sucking calves out of the midst of the herd; who applaud at the sound of the musical instruments; they reckon them as stable, and not as fleeting, who drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments, but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: Trypho responded, "It seems to me that those who claim he was a human being, chosen and anointed, and thus became the Christ, are making a more persuasive case than you are. After all, we all expect the Christ to be born a man from men, and for Elijah to come and anoint him. But if this man is the Christ, one must know in every way that he was born a human being from humans. Since Elijah has not come, however, I conclude that this man is not the Christ." I then questioned him further: "Does not the Scripture say through Zechariah that Elijah will come before the great and fearful day of the Lord?" (Zechariah). He answered, "Certainly." "If, then, the Word compels us to acknowledge that two comings of Christ were prophesied—one in which he will appear suffering, inglorious, and unknown, and another in which he will come in glory as the judge of all, as has been demonstrated in many of our previous discussions—should we not understand that the Word of God announced Elijah as a forerunner before that fearful and great day, that is, before the second coming of Christ?" He replied, "Certainly."

"Our Lord," I continued, "handed down this very teaching in his doctrines, declaring that Elijah would come. We know this will take place when our Lord Jesus Christ is about to arrive in glory from heaven. The Spirit of God that was in Elijah went before him in John, a prophet who arose in your nation; after him, no other prophet appeared among you. Sitting by the Jordan River, John cried out, 'I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one who is stronger than I is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire. His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.' Your king Herod threw this prophet into prison. When Herod's birthday was celebrated and the daughter of his sister danced in a way that pleased him, he promised to give her whatever she asked. Prompted by her mother, she requested the head of John the Baptist, who was in prison. Herod sent an executioner and ordered John's head to be brought on a platter. Therefore, our Christ also spoke to those who insisted that Elijah must come before the Christ: 'Elijah will indeed come and restore all things; but I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they pleased.' And it is written, 'Then the disciples understood that he was speaking to them about John the Baptist.'"

Trypho objected, "You seem to me to be saying something paradoxical: that the prophetic Spirit of God that was in Elijah also came to be in John." I answered, "Does it not seem to you that the very same thing happened with Joshua son of Nun, who succeeded Moses in leadership? When God told Moses to lay his hands on Joshua, he said, 'Shall I not put upon him the Spirit that is in you?' (Numbers 11:25). He agreed. Just as God transferred the Spirit that was in Moses to Joshua while Moses was still alive, so also God was able to bring the Spirit from Elijah to John. This was so that, just as the first coming of Christ was inglorious, the first coming of the Spirit that was always in Elijah might also be understood as inglorious, like Christ's. For it is said that the Lord fought against Amalek with a hidden hand, and you will not deny that Amalek fell. But if the Scripture says that Amalek will be fought only in the glorious coming of Christ, what fruit does the word have that says, 'The Lord fights Amalek with a hidden hand'? You can perceive that the hidden power of God became the crucified Christ, whom even the demons fear, and all the authorities and powers of the earth."

greek: Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Ἐμοὶ μὲν δοκοῦσιν, εἶπεν, οἱ λέγοντες ἄνθρωπον γεγονέναι αὐτὸν καὶ κατ᾿ ἐκλογὴν κεχρῖσθαι καὶ Χριστὸν γεγονέναι πιθανώτερον ὑμῶν λέγειν, τῶν ταῦτα ἅπερ φῂς λεγόντων· καὶ γὰρ πάντες ἡμεῖς τὸν Χριστὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων προσδοκῶμεν γενήσεσθαι , καὶ τὸν Ἡλίαν χρῖσαι αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα. Ἐὰν δὲ οὗτος φαίνηται ὢν ὁ Χριστός, ἄνθρωπον μὲν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γενόμενον ἐκ παντὸς ἐπίστασθαι δεῖ. Ἐκ δὲ τοῦ μηδὲ Ἡλίαν ἐληλυθέναι οὐδὲ τοῦτον ἀποφαίνομαι εἶναι. Κἀγὼ πάλιν ἐπυθόμην αὐτοῦ· Οὐχὶ Ἡλίαν φησὶν ὁ λόγος διὰ Ζαχαρίου ἐλεύσεσθαι πρὸ τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης καὶ φοβερᾶς ταύτης τοῦ κυρίου ; Κἀκεῖνος ἀπεκρίνατο· Μάλιστα. Ἐὰν οὖν ὁ λόγος ἀναγκάζῃ ὁμολογεῖν ὅτι δύο παρουσίαι τοῦ Χριστοῦ προεφητεύοντο γενησόμεναι, μία μέν. ἐν ᾖ παθητός καὶ ἄτιμος καὶ ἀειδὴς φανήσεται , ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἔνδοξος καὶ κριτὴς ἁπάντων ἐλεύσεται , ὡς καὶ ἐν πολλοῖς τοῖς προλελεγμένοις ἀποδέδεικται, οὐχὶ τῆς φοβερᾶς καὶ μεγάλης ἡμέρας τουτέστι τῆς δευτέρας παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, πρόοδον γενήσεσθαι τὸν Ἡλίαν νοήσομεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ κεκηρυχέναι; Μάλιστα, ἀπεκρίνατο. Καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος οὖν κύριος, ἔφην, τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἐν τοῖς διδάγμασιν αὐτοῦ παρέδωκε γενησόμενον, εἰπὼν καὶ Ἡλίαν ἐλεύσεσθαι · καὶ ἡμεῖς τοῦτο ἐπιστάμεθα γενησόμενον, ὅταν μέλλῃ ἐν δόξῃ ἐξ οὐρανῶν παραγίνεσθαι ὁ ἡμέτερος κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὗ καὶ τῆς πρώτης φανερώσεως κῆρυξ προῆλθε τὸ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ γενόμενον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν Ἰωάννῃ , τῷ γενομένῳ ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν προφήτῃ, μεθ᾿ ὃν οὐδεὶς ἕτερος λοιπὸν παρ᾿ ὑμῖν ἐφάνη προφήτης· ὅστις ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην ποταμὸν καθεζόμενος ἐβόα· Ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ὲν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ἥξει δὲ ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί. Οὗ τὸ πτύον αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν σῖτον συνάξει εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ . Καὶ τοῦτον αὐτὸν τὸν προφήτην συνεκεκλείκει ὁ βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν Ἡρώδης εἰς φυλακήν. καὶ γενεσίων ἡμέρας τελουμένης, ὀρχουμένης τῆς ἐξαδελφῆς αὐτοῦ εὐαρέστως αὐτῷ, εἶπεν αὐτῇ αἰτήσασθαι ὃ ἐὰν βούληται. Καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῆς παιδὸς ὑπέβαλεν αὐτῇ αἰτήσασθαι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· καὶ αἰτησάσης ἔπεμψε καὶ ἐπὶ πίνακι ἐνεχθῆναι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου ἐκέλευσε . Διὸ καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος Χριστὸς εἰρήκει ἐπὶ γῆς τότε τοῖς λέγουσι πρὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἡλίαν δεῖν ἐλθεῖν· Ἡλίας μὲν ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἡλίας ἤδη ἦλθε, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν, ἀλλ᾿ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν. Καὶ γέγραπται ὅτι Τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς . Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Καὶ τοῦτο παράδοξον λέγειν μοι δοκεῖς, ὅτι τὸ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ γενόμενον προφητικὸν πνεῦμα καὶ ἐν Ἰωάννῃ γέγονε. Κἀγὼ πρὸς ταῦτα· Οὐ δοκεῖ σοι ἐπὶ Ἰησοῦν, τὸν τοῦ Ναυῆ, τὸν διαδεξάμενον τὴν λαοηγησίαν μετὰ Μωσέα. τὸ αὐτὸ γεγονέναι, ὅτε ἐρρέθη τῷ Μωσεῖ ἐπιθεῖναι τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὰς χεῖρας , εἰπόντος αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ· Κἀγὼ μεταθήσω ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐν σοὶ ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν ; Κἀκεῖνος· Μάλιστα. Ὡς οὖν, φημί. ἔτι ὄντος τότε ἐν ἀνθρώποις τοῦ Μωσέως, μετέθηκεν ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐν Μωσεῖ πνεύματος, οὕτως καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἡλίου ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐλθεῖν ὁ θεὸς δυνατὸς ἦν ποιῆσαι. ἵνα, ὥσπερ ὁ Χριστὸς τῇ πρώτῃ παρουσίᾳ ἄδοξος ἐφάνη, οὕτως καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ πάντοτε καθαρεύοντος, ὡς τοῦ Χριστοῦ. ἄδοξος ἡ πρώτη παρουσία νοηθῇ. Κρυφίᾳ γὰρ χειρὶ ὁ κύριος πολεμεῖν τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ εἴρηται , καὶ ὅτι ἔπεσεν ὁ Ἀμαλὴκ οὐκ ἀρνήσεσθε. Εἰ δὲ ἐν τῇ ἐνδόξῳ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πολεμηθήσεσθαι τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ μόνον λέγεται, ποῖος καρπὸς ἔσται τοῦ λόγου. ὅς φησι· Κρυφίᾳ χειρὶ ὁ θεὸς πολεμεῖ τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ: Νοῆσαι δύνασθε ὅτι κρυφία δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ γέγονε τῷ σταυρωθέντι Χριστῷ, ὃν καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια φρίσσει καὶ πᾶσαι ἁπλῶς αἱ ἀρχαὶ καὶ ἐξουσίαι τῆς γῆς.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: I therefore expect to be plotted against by one of those already named and brought to the cross, perhaps even by Crescens, the lover of wisdom and lover of fame. He is not worthy to be called a philosopher, for he publicly testifies against us concerning things he does not understand, charging that Christians are atheists and impious, and he does this for the favor and pleasure of the many who have been led astray. If he reviles us without having encountered the teachings of Christ, he is thoroughly wicked and far worse than private citizens, who often refrain from discussing or bearing false witness about things they do not know. But if he has encountered those teachings and failed to grasp their greatness, or if he grasped it yet acts in this way so as not to be suspected of allegiance, he is all the more ignoble and thoroughly wicked, subordinate to private, irrational glory and fear. I want you to know that I approached him, put certain questions to him, and discovered and demonstrated that he truly knows nothing. If the records of our conversations have not yet reached you, I am ready to share those questions with you again; that too would be a royal work. But if my questions and his answers have already become known to you, it is clear to you that he knows nothing of our doctrine; or if he does know, he does not dare say so to his hearers, any more than Socrates did, as I said before. He shows himself not a lover of wisdom but a lover of fame, one who does not even honor the Socratic principle that is worthy of honor: that no man is to be honored above the truth. And it is impossible for a Cynic, who has made indifference his goal, to know the good apart from indifference.

excerpts.author: Justin Martyr
english: I will answer briefly so that no one can repeat the charge leveled by those who pass for philosophers: that our teaching on the eternal fire awaiting the unrighteous is nothing but fable and scare‑tactic, and that we urge virtue only from fear, not because it is good and pleasing in itself. If that charge were true, then either God does not exist, or He exists but cares nothing for humanity; virtue and wickedness would be empty names, and, as I have already said, lawmakers would be punishing transgressors of good laws unjustly. But those lawmakers and their Father are not unjust; they teach through the Word that we should do the same righteous things, so those who agree with them are not unjust either.

If someone objects by pointing to the diversity of human laws — claiming that what one people calls good another calls shameful, and vice versa — let him also hear the answer to that objection. We know that wicked angels have established laws that mirror their own wickedness, and that people who become like them take pleasure in those laws. Right reason, passing over all opinions, does not prove that every doctrine is good; it distinguishes the bad from the good. Therefore the same and similar things will be said to such objectors, and at greater length if need be. For now, I return to the matter at hand.

Τανῦν δὲ ἐπὶ τὸ προκείμενον ἀνέρχομαι.

english: Whosoever confesses that one God is the author of both Testaments, and diligently reads the Scriptures in company with the presbyters of the Church, is a true spiritual disciple; and he will rightly understand and interpret all that the prophets have declared respecting Christ and the liberty of the New Testament.

1. A spiritual disciple of this sort truly receiving the Spirit of God , who was from the beginning, in all the dispensations of God , present with mankind , and announced things future, revealed things present, and narrated things past — [such a man] does indeed judge all men , but is himself judged by no man. For he judges the Gentiles , who serve the creature more than the Creator, Romans 1:21 and with a reprobate mind spend all their labour on vanity. And he also judges the Jews , who do not accept of the word of liberty, nor are willing to go forth free, although they have a Deliverer present [with them]; but they pretend, at a time unsuitable [for such conduct], to serve, [with observances] beyond [those required by] the law, God who stands in need of nothing, and do not recognise the advent of Christ , which He accomplished for the salvation of men , nor are willing to understand that all the prophets announced His two advents: the one, indeed, in which He became a man subject to stripes, and knowing what it is to bear infirmity, Isaiah 53:3 and sat upon the foal of an ass, Zechariah 9:9 and was a stone rejected by the builders, and was led as a sheep to the slaughter, Isaiah 53:7 and by the stretching forth of His hands destroyed Amalek; Exodus 17:11 while He gathered from the ends of the earth into His Father's fold the children who were scattered abroad, Isaiah 11:12 and remembered His own dead ones who had formerly fallen asleep, and came down to them that He…

2. Moreover, he shall also examine the doctrine of Marcion , [inquiring] how he holds that there are two gods, separated from each other by an infinite distance. Or how can he be good who draws away men that do not belong to him from him who made them, and calls them into his own kingdom? And why is his goodness, which does not save all [thus], defective? Also, why does he, indeed, seem to be good as respects men, but most unjust with regard to him who made men, inasmuch as he deprives him of his possessions? Moreover, how could the Lord, with any justice , if He belonged to another father, have acknowledged the bread to be His body, while He took it from that creation to which we belong, and affirmed the mixed cup to be His blood? And why did He acknowledge Himself to be the Son of man , if He had not gone through that birth which belongs to a human being? How, too, could He forgive us those sins for which we are answerable to our Maker and God? And how, again, supposing that He was not flesh, but was a man merely in appearance, could He have been crucified, and could blood and water have issued from His pierced side? John 19:34 What body, moreover, was it that those who buried Him consigned to the tomb? And what was that which rose again from the dead?

3. [This spiritual man] shall also judge all the followers of Valentinus , because they do indeed confess with the tongue one God the Father , and that all things derive their existence from Him, but do at the same time maintain that He who formed all things is the fruit of an apostasy or defect. [He shall judge them, too, because] they do in like manner confess with the tongue one Lord Jesus Christ , the Son of God , but assign in their [system of] doctrine a production of his own to the Only-begotten, one of his own also to the Word, another to Christ , and yet another to the Saviour; so that, according to them, all these beings are indeed said [in Scripture to be], as it were, one; [while they maintain], notwithstanding, that each one of them should be understood [to exist] separately [from the rest], and to have [had] his own special origin, according to his peculiar conjunction. english: All these facts are confirmed by every ancient, approved, and authoritative Scripture, and by the testimony of those who saw John face to face; reason itself also teaches that the number of the beast's name, calculated according to the Greek method through the letters that compose it, comes to six hundred sixty-six—that is, equal tens of hundreds and equal hundreds of units. The digit six, similarly preserved, displays the recapitulations of his apostasy: the one that began at the start, the one in the middle times, and the one that will occur at the end. I cannot understand how certain persons went astray by following a foolish error, mutilating the middle of the number of the name by subtracting fifty so that they could make a single decade stand for six decades. I judge this to have been a scribal sin, as often happens, because numbers are also expressed by letters, and the Greek letter that signifies sixty was easily expanded into the Greek iota. Afterward some accepted this without investigation; others simply and foolishly used the number ten; still others dared to search out names that contained the false number of error. To those who acted merely out of simplicity and without malice we believe God will grant pardon. But as for those who, for the sake of empty glory, establish names containing the false number and declare their own invented name to be that of the coming one—they will not escape loss, because they have deceived both themselves and those who believe them. The loss itself is to fall away from the truth and to treat what does not exist as real. Moreover, adding to or taking away from Scripture brings no small penalty, which such a person must inevitably incur. Another danger, by no means slight, will also follow those who falsely presume to know his name: if they think one thing while he arrives with another, they will easily be seduced by him, as though he were not yet present—the very one we ought to beware of.

Therefore such people must learn and return to the true number of the name, lest they be classed as false prophets. Knowing the firm number announced by Scripture—six hundred sixty-six—let them first endure the division of the kingdom into ten. Then, while those ten reign and begin to set their affairs in order and expand their dominion, the one who comes unexpectedly and claims the kingdom for himself will terrify those former rulers; having a name that contains the aforesaid number, he must be recognized as the abomination of desolation. The Apostle also says: when they say, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction will come upon them. Not only his sudden coming, but also the tribe of six by which he will come, is revealed: "The voice of the neighing of his horses will shake the whole earth; he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, the city and those who dwell in it." Because of this, that tribe is not counted among the saved in the Apocalypse. It is therefore more certain and without danger to await the fulfillment of prophecy than to speculate and guess at any names; for many names can be found that possess the predicted number, and yet the same question would remain. If many names are discovered bearing this number—the one the coming one will bear—it will still be asked which one is his.

We say these things not because of a shortage of names that have the number of his name, but out of reverence and zeal for the truth. The name Euanthas possesses the number in question, yet we affirm nothing about it. The name itself totals six hundred sixty-six, and it is very plausible, since this final kingdom bears that name; the Latins are the ones who now reign, but we do not boast in this. Also the name Titan, written with two Greek vowels e and i, contains the predicted number in itself and is worthy of confidence. It consists of six letters, with single syllables made of three letters each, and it is ancient and set apart; for none of the kings who belong to us has been called Titan, nor do the idols publicly worshiped among Greeks and barbarians bear that name. Many regard the name as divine, so that even the sun is called Titan by those who now hold power. The name also carries a certain display of vengeance and retribution, since he pretends to avenge those who have been mistreated. It is likewise ancient, trustworthy, and royal—yet more tyrannical. Because the name Titan carries such weight of persuasion and verisimilitude, we gather from many indications that perhaps the coming one will be called Titan; nevertheless we will not risk it, nor will we assertively pronounce that he will bear this name. We know that if it had been necessary to proclaim his name openly at the present time, it would have been published by the one who also saw the Apocalypse; for the vision was not seen long ago, but almost in our own century, at the end of Domitian's reign.

Now the number of the name is shown so that we may beware of the one who is coming, knowing who he is; but the name itself is kept silent, because it is not worthy to be proclaimed by the Holy Spirit. If it had been proclaimed by Him, perhaps it would have endured for a long time. But now, since the beast is not, yet will ascend from the abyss and go to perdition as though he did not exist, neither is his name proclaimed; for the name of that which is not is not proclaimed. When the Antichrist has established all things in this world, he will reign for three years and six months and will sit in the temple at Jerusalem. Then the Lord will come from heaven in clouds, in the glory of the Father, sending him and those who obey him into the lake of fire, but bringing the times of the kingdom to the just—that is, rest, sanctifying the seventh day—and restoring the promise of inheritance to Abraham. In that kingdom the Lord says many will come from east and west and will recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english:
If some attempt to allegorize these matters, they will not be found consistent with themselves in every respect, for the very words themselves will convict them. When the cities of the nations are deserted, when houses stand empty because no one lives in them, and the earth is left desolate, Isaiah declares: "Behold, the day of the Lord is coming, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger, to make the land a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it" (Isaiah 13:9). He says again: "Let him be taken away, that he may not see the glory of the Lord" (Isaiah 13:19), and when these things have come to pass, God will prolong the days of men, and the deserted ones will multiply on the earth. They will build houses and inhabit them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit. These words speak plainly of the resurrection of the just, which takes place after the coming of the Antichrist and the destruction of all the nations that exist under his rule. In that time the just will reign on the earth, growing through the vision of the Lord and becoming accustomed through him to receive the glory of God and the unity of spiritual things in the kingdom. Those whom Christ finds on the earth, waiting for him from heaven and having endured tribulation, who also escaped the hands of the wicked — these are the ones of whom the prophet says, "And the deserted ones will be multiplied on the earth." As many believers as God has prepared for this, to be left on the earth and to serve under the Kingdom of the Saints, ministering to this Jerusalem and the kingdom within it, Jeremiah the prophet foretold, saying: "Look around toward the east, O Jerusalem, and see the joy that comes to you from God himself. Behold, your sons whom you sent away shall come, gathered from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of your God. Put off the garment of your mourning and affliction, O Jerusalem, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from your God. Wrap yourself in the robe of righteousness from your God; place on your head the crown of eternal glory. For God will show your splendor to all under heaven. Your name shall be called by God forever: peace of righteousness and glory to those who worship God. Arise, O Jerusalem, stand on the height; look toward the east and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them. For they went out on foot, led away by enemies; but God will bring them back to you, carried in glory as upon a royal throne. For God has decreed that every high mountain shall be made low, and the everlasting hills, and the valleys filled up, to make level ground, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God. The woods and every fragrant tree have shaded Israel at God's command. For God will lead Israel with joy, in the light of his glory, with the mercy and righteousness that come from him.

But these things cannot be understood as belonging to some supercelestial realm; for God says he will show Jerusalem's splendor to all under heaven — yet this happens in the times of the Kingdom, when the earth has been reclaimed by Christ and Jerusalem rebuilt according to the pattern of the Jerusalem above, of which Isaiah says: "Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are continually before me." The Apostle writes to the Galatians in the same way: "But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother" (Galatians 4:26) — not from the thought of some errant Aeon, nor by any virtue that has emanated from the Pleroma and the Prunicus, but from the Jerusalem that has been depicted in the hands of God. And John saw this Jerusalem descending, new, upon the earth in the Apocalypse. For after the times of the Kingdom, he says: "Then I saw a great white throne and him who was seated on it. From his presence earth and sky fled away, and no place was found for them" (Revelation 20:11). He describes the general resurrection and judgment: "The sea gave up the dead who were in it, Death and Hades gave up the dead who were in them, and they were judged, each one of them, according to what they had done. Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death, the lake of fire. And if anyone's name was not found written in the book of life, he was thrown into the lake of fire" (Revelation 20:13-15). This is what is called Gehenna, which the Lord said is eternal fire. And after these things John says: "Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. And I saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, 'Behold, the dwelling place of God is with man. He will dwell with them, and they will be his people, and God himself will be with them as their God. He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away'" (Revelation 21:1-4). Isaiah says the same: "They shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away." This is what the Apostle declared: "The form of this world is passing away." So also the Lord says: "Heaven and earth will pass away." When these things therefore pass away on the earth, the Lord's disciple John says there will be a new and higher Jerusalem on the earth, like a bride adorned for her husband; and this is the tabernacle of God, in which God will dwell with men. The image of this Jerusalem is the one that existed on the former earth, in Jerusalem, where the just are prepared for incorruption and made ready for salvation. Moses received the pattern of this tabernacle on the mountain; and nothing can be allegorized — all things are firm and true, possessing substance, made by God for the enjoyment of just men. For just as God is truly the One who raises man, so also he truly rises from the dead, and not allegorically, as we have shown through so many proofs. And just as he truly rises, so also will he truly prepare incorruption, and will increase, and will flourish in the times of the kingdom, that he may become the perfect glory of the Father. Then, when all things have been renewed, he will truly dwell in the city of God. For the One seated on the throne says: "Behold, I make all things new." And the Lord says: "Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true." And he said to me: "It is done." And this is according to reason.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: Indeed, what He says—'How often I wanted to gather your sons, and you did not want to'—revealed the ancient law of human freedom, because God made man free from the beginning, possessing his own power just as his own soul, to use God's judgment voluntarily and not under compulsion from God; for force does not come from God, but good judgment is always present to him, and because of this counsel He gives good counsel to all.

He placed in man the power of choice, just as in angels (for angels are rational), so that those who obeyed are justly good, possessing what was given by God but kept by themselves, while those who did not obey will not justly find the good and will receive the penalty they deserve, because God gave the good kindly but they did not keep it carefully nor count it precious but despised the surpassing goodness; therefore, rejecting the good and as if spurning it, all will justly incur God's judgment, just as the Apostle Paul testified in the epistle to the Romans, saying: 'Do you despise the riches of His kindness and patience and forbearance?' (Romans 2:4).

And: 'Glory and honor to everyone who does good' (Romans 2:10). Therefore God gave the good, just as the Apostle testifies in the same epistle, and those who do it will receive glory and honor because they did the good when they could have not done it, but those who do not do it will receive just judgment because they did not do the good when they could have done it.

This shows that some are not good by nature and some bad, but that the good lies in human choice; for if some were naturally good and some naturally bad, neither would the good be praiseworthy, since they were made so, nor would the bad be blameworthy, since they were constituted so; but since all share the same nature and are able to retain and do good and able again to lose it and not do it, justly among sensible men—how much more before God—some are praised and receive worthy testimony of their good choice and perseverance, while others are accused and receive worthy loss because they rejected the just and good.

And therefore the prophets exhorted men to do justice and work good, as we have shown through many passages, because this lies in us and because of much negligence we fell into oblivion and need good counsel; for this reason the good God gives good counsel through the prophets.

And for this reason the Lord also said: 'Let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven' (Matthew 5:16); and: 'Take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with carousing and drunkenness and the cares of this life' (Luke 21:34); and: 'Let your loins be girded and your lamps burning, and be like men waiting for their Lord when He returns from the wedding, that when He knocks they may open to Him. Blessed is that servant whom His Lord finds so doing when He comes' (Luke 12:35-37); and again: 'The servant who knows his Lord's will and does not do it will be beaten with many stripes' (Luke 12:47); and: 'Why do you call Me Lord, Lord, and not do what I say?' (Luke 6:46); and again: 'But if that servant says in his heart, My Lord delays his coming, and begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink and get drunk, the Lord of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and appoint his portion with the hypocrites' (Luke 12:45-46).
All such things show that man is free and in his own power, and that God instructs with counsel, exhorting us to subjection to Him and turning us away from unbelief, yet not compelling by violence.

excerpts.author: Irenaeus
english: In this world some run to the light and, through faith, join themselves to God, while others turn away from the light and cut themselves off from Him. Therefore the Word of God comes, bringing a dwelling fit for everyone: for those who stand in the light, that they may enjoy it and the good things found in it; for those who linger in darkness, that they may share in the calamities that belong to them. That is why He declares that those on the right will be called into the kingdom of the Father, but those on the left will be dispatched into eternal fire, because they have stripped themselves of every good thing.

That is also why the Apostle says: because they refused to welcome the love of God that would have saved them, God will send them a powerful delusion so that they believe the lie, with the result that all who did not believe the truth but gave their consent to wickedness will be condemned. When this man arrives, he will gather up the whole apostasy into himself by his own judgment; he will act entirely by his own will and choice; and he will sit in the temple of God, demanding the worship due to Christ from those he has deceived. Consequently, they will be justly thrown into the lake of fire. Yet God, in His providence, foreknows all things and, at the appointed time, sends this very man so that they may believe falsehood, so that all who refused the truth and embraced iniquity may be judged.

John foretold his coming in the Apocalypse: The beast I saw resembled a leopard, its feet were like a bear's, its mouth like a lion's; the dragon handed over to it his own power, his throne, and great authority. One of its heads appeared to have been mortally wounded, but the death-blow was healed, and the whole earth marveled and followed the beast. They worshiped the dragon because he had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast itself, crying, "Who is like the beast, and who can fight against it?" It was given a mouth that uttered arrogant words and blasphemies, and authority to act for forty-two months. It opened its mouth to blaspheme God -- to slander His name, His dwelling, and those who dwell in heaven. It was granted authority over every tribe, people, language, and nation, and all earth-dwellers whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world worshiped it. If anyone has ears, let him hear. If anyone is destined for captivity, into captivity he goes; if anyone is destined for the sword, by the sword he must die. Here is the endurance and faith of the saints.

Then John speaks of the beast's lieutenant, also called the false prophet: he spoke like a dragon and exercised all the authority of the first beast on its behalf. He compels the earth and its inhabitants to worship the first beast, whose fatal wound had been healed. He performs great signs, even calling fire down from heaven to earth before men's eyes, and by these signs he deceives the earth-dwellers so that they do not suppose he works by divine power but by sorcery. No wonder: demons and apostate spirits serve him, and through them he performs signs that seduce the inhabitants of the earth. He will order an image of the beast to be made, breathe life into it so that it can speak, and put to death all who refuse to worship it. He will cause a mark to be placed on the right hand or forehead of every person, so that no one can buy or sell without the beast's name or the number of its name. That number is six hundred sixty-six -- six times one hundred, plus ten, plus seven, plus six -- summing up the whole apostasy accomplished in six thousand years. For as many days as the world took to make, so many thousands of years it runs.

That is why Scripture says: "The heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host. On the sixth day God finished the work He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work." This account of the past is also a prophecy of the future. A day of the Lord is like a thousand years; in six days creation was finished, so it is clear that the consummation comes in the sixth millennium. Throughout all time, man -- formed at the beginning by the hands of God, that is, by the Son and the Spirit -- is being shaped according to the image and likeness of God. The chaff, which is apostasy, is cast away; the wheat, those who bear fruit in faith toward God, is gathered into the storehouse. Therefore tribulation is necessary for those who are being saved, so that, broken and refined and sprinkled through patience with the Word of God and kindled by it, they may become fit for the King's banquet. As one of our own said when condemned to the beasts for the sake of martyrdom in God: "I am the grain of Christ; I am ground by the teeth of beasts, that I may be found the pure bread of God." All things were made for the benefit of humanity, and the deceits, wickedness, and apostate power of the Antichrist were prefigured from the flood onward, and afterward in the persecution of Ananias, Azarias, and Misael.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: Since the sons of Israel insist we are wrong to accept Christ, who has already come, let us prove from their own Scriptures that the promised Christ has indeed arrived—even though the chronology of Daniel's prophecy already makes this clear. He had to be born in Bethlehem of Judah, for the prophet writes: "And you, Bethlehem, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel" (Micah 5:2). If that ruler has not yet been born, he still must arise from the tribe of Judah and from Bethlehem; yet today not a single descendant of Israel remains in Bethlehem, and Jews are forbidden even to dwell in its surrounding territory—fulfilling the prophet's words: "Your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire"—that is, what befell them in wartime; "your land is devoured by foreigners before your eyes, desolate and overthrown by alien peoples." Elsewhere the prophet declares: "You will see the King in his beauty"—meaning Christ working mighty deeds in the glory of God the Father—"and your eyes will see the land from afar" (cf. Daniel 9:26): because of your merits, after Jerusalem's capture you were barred from entering your land, permitted only to gaze on it from a distance. "Your soul will meditate on terror"—that is, at the moment they suffered their own destruction. So how can the ruler be born from Judah and come forth from Bethlehem, as the divine prophetic scrolls announce, when no Israelite stock remains there today from which Christ could spring? If, as the Jews claim, he has not yet come, then when he does begin to come, from where will he be anointed? The law forbade the preparation of royal chrism in captivity. And if there is now no anointing for them, as Daniel foretold—"The anointing shall be cut off"—then no anointing exists, because the temple is gone, along with the horn from which kings were anointed. If there is no anointing, how will the ruler born in Bethlehem be anointed? Or how will he proceed from Bethlehem when not a single descendant of Israel remains there?
