latin: Igitur, quoniam filii Israel affirmant nos errare recipiendo Christum, qui jam venit, praescribamus eis ex ipsis Scripturis jam venisse Christum qui praedicabatur; quamvis ex temporibus Danielis praedicantis probaverimus jam venisse Christum, qui nuntiabatur. Nasci enim eum oportuit in Bethlehem Judae; sic enim scriptum est in propheta: Et tu Bethlehem, non minima es in ducibus Juda: ex te enim exiet dux qui pascat populum meum Israel. Si autem adhuc natus non est qui processurus dux de tribu Juda ex Bethlehem nuntiabatur, oportet enim eum de tribu Juda et a Bethlehem procedere; animadvertimus autem nunc neminem de genere Israel in civitate Bethlehem remansisse, et exinde quod interdictum est ne in confinio ipsius regionis demoretur quisquam Judaeorum, ut hoc quoque esset adimpletum per prophetam: Terra vestra deserta, civitates vestrae igni exustae, id est quod belli tempore eis evenerit; regionem vestram in conspectu vestro exteri comedent, et deserta et subversa erit a populis alienis. Et alio loco sic per prophetam dicitur: Regem cum claritate videbitis, id est Christum facientem virtutes in gloria Dei patris, et oculi vestri videbunt terram de longinquo: quod vobis pro meritis vestris post expugnationem Hierusalem, prohibitis ingredi in terram vestram, de longinquo eam oculis tantum videre permissum est. Anima, inquit, vestra meditabitur timorem. scilicet quo tempore excidium sui passi sunt. Quomodo igitur nascetur dux de Judaea, et quatenus procedet de Bethlehem, sicut divina prophetarum volumina nuntiant, cum nullus omnino sit illic in hodiernum derelictus ex Israel, cujus ex stirpe possit nasci Christus? Si enim, secundum Judaeos, adhuc non venit, cum venire coeperit, unde ungetur? Lex enim praecepit, in captivitate non licere unctionem chrismatis regalis confici. Si autem jam nec unctio est illis, ut Daniel prophetavit; dicit enim: Exterminabitur unctio: ergo jam non est illic unctio, quia nec templum ubi erat cornu de quo reges ungebantur. Si ergo non est unctio, unde ungetur dux qui nascetur in Bethlehem? aut quomodo procedet de Bethlehem, cum de germine Israel nullus omnino sit in Bethlehem?

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: We should rather keep in mind both the Lord's pronouncements and the apostolic letters, which foretold future heresies to us and defined them as things to be avoided (Matt 7:15); and just as we do not fear that those heresies exist, so we should not be surprised that they can do the very thing for which they are to be avoided. The Lord teaches that many will come in sheep's clothing as rapacious wolves. What are these sheepskins, if not the external surface of the Christian name? Who are the rapacious wolves, if not cunning minds and spirits lurking outwardly to harass Christ's flock? Who are the false prophets, if not false preachers? Who are the false apostles, if not adulterous evangelists? Who are the antichrists, both now and always, if not rebels against Christ? Heresies exist now, troubling the Church with the perversity of their doctrines no less than the Antichrist will persecute it then with the atrocity of his persecutions; the only difference is that persecution makes martyrs, while heresy makes only apostates. And therefore heresies also had to exist, so that the approved might be revealed — both those who stand firm in persecutions and those who do not deviate into heresies. For it does no good to regard as approved those who change their faith into heresy: just as, on the other hand, they interpret the matter for themselves, because He said elsewhere: "Examine all things; hold fast to what is good" (1 Thess 5:21). As if it were not possible, after examining all things poorly, to fall by error into the choice of some evil.

latin: Quin potius memores simus tam dominicarum pronuntiationum, quam apostolicarum litterarum, quae nobis et futuras haereses praenuntiarunt, et fugiendas praefinierunt; et sicut esse illas non expavescimus, ita posse id, propter quod fugiendae sunt, non miremur. Instruit Dominus multos esse venturos, sub pellibus ovium, rapaces lupos. Quaenam istae sunt pelles ovium, nisi nominis christiani extrinsecus superficies? qui lupi rapaces, nisi sensus et spiritus subdoli, ad infestandum gregem Christi extrinsecus delitescentes? qui pseudoprophetae sunt, nisi falsi praedicatores? qui pseudapostoli, nisi adulteri evangelizatores? qui antichristi interim et semper, nisi Christi rebelles? Nunc sunt haereses, non minus doctrinarum perversitate Ecclesiam lacessentes, quam tunc Antichristus persecutionum atrocitate persequetur: nisi quod persecutio et martyras facit, haeresis apostatas tantum. Et ideo haereses quoque oportebat esse, ut probabiles quique manifestarentur, tam qui in persecutionibus steterint, quam qui ad haereses non exorbitaverint. Neque enim eos probabiles intelligi juvat, qui in haeresim fidem demutant: sicut ex diverso sibi interpretantur, quia dixit alibi: Omnia examinate, quod bonum est tenete. Quasi non liceat, omnibus male examinatis, in electionem alicujus mali impingere per errorem.

excerpts.citation: Tertullian — An Answer to the Jews 8
excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: Therefore we must pin down the times of Christ's predicted and future birth, his passion, and the extermination of the city of Jerusalem—that is, its devastation. Daniel says both the holy city and the holy one will be destroyed when the coming leader arrives, and the pinnacle will be destroyed until the end (Daniel 9:24-27). So we must investigate the times of the coming leader Christ in Daniel; once we calculate them, we will prove he came—not only from the prescribed times, but from the fitting signs and from his works. We prove this from the events announced to happen after his advent, so we may believe all things were fulfilled just as they were foreseen.

Thus Daniel prophesied about him to show both when and at what time he would liberate the nations, and that this city would be destroyed after Christ's passion. Here is what he says: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, of Median stock, who ruled the Chaldean kingdom, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years. While I was still praying, the man Gabriel—the one I had seen in the vision at the beginning—came flying and touched me, about the time of the evening sacrifice. He gave me understanding, spoke with me, and said: "Daniel, I have now come to give you insight. At the start of your plea the word went out, and I have come to tell you, because you are a man of desires. Consider the word and understand the vision."

Seventy weeks have been decreed for your people and for the holy city, until sin grows old, sins are sealed up, injustices are atoned for, and everlasting righteousness is brought in, so that vision and prophet may be sealed and the Holy of Holies anointed (Daniel 9:24-27). You will know, discern, and understand from the issuing of the word: from restoring and rebuilding Jerusalem until Christ the leader comes, seven and a half weeks and sixty-two and a half weeks. It will be restored and built with joy, and a wall, and the times will be renewed. After those sixty-two weeks, the anointing will be cut off and will be no more; the city and the holy place will be destroyed when the leader comes, and they will be swept away as in a flood until the end of the war, which is decreed to the very end. And he will confirm the covenant with many (Daniel 9:24-27).

latin: Itaque requirenda tempora praedictae et futurae nativitatis Christi, et passionis ejus, et exterminii civitatis Hierusalem, id est, vastationis ejus. Dicit enim Daniel et civitatem sanctam et sanctum exterminari cum duce venturo, et destrui pinnaculum usque ad interitum. Venturi itaque Christi ducis sunt tempora requirenda, quae investigabimus in Daniele: quibus computatis, probabimus venisse cum, etiam ex temporibus praescriptis, et ex signis competentibus, et ex operationibus ejus: quae probamus ex consequentibus quae post adventum ejus futura adnuntiabantur, ut tam adimpleta omnia quam prospecta credamus. Sic igitur de eo Daniel praedicavit, ut et quando et quo in tempore gentes esset liberaturus, ostenderet, et quoniam post passionem Christi ista civitas exterminari haberet. Dicit enim sic: In primo anno sub Dario filio Assueri ex semine Medorum, qui regnavit super regnum Chaldaeorum, ego Daniel intellexi in libris numerum annorum. Et adhuc me loquente in oratione, ecce vir Gabriel, quem vidi in visione in principio, volans, et tetigit me, quasi hora sacrificii vespertini, et intelligere fecit me, et locutus est mecum, et dixit: «Daniel, nunc exivi imbuere te intelligentia, in principio obsecrationis tuae exivit sermo. Et ego veni ut annuntiem tibi, quia vir desideriorum tu es, et cogita in verbo, et intellige in visione.» Septuaginta hebdomadae breviatae sunt super plebem tuam, et super civitatem sanctam, quoadusque inveteretur delictum, et signentur peccata, et exorentur injustitiae, et inducatur justitia aeterna, ut et signetur visio et prophetes, et ut ungatur Sanctus sanctorum. Et scies, et perspicies et intelliges a profectione sermonis, integrando et reaedificando Hierusalem usque ad Christum ducem, hebdomadas septem et dimidiam, et septuaginta duas et dimidiam: et convertet, et aedificabitur in laetitiam, et convallationem, et innovabuntur tempora: et post hebdomadas has septuaginta duas, et exterminabitur unctio, et non erit: et civitatem et sanctum exterminabit cum duce adveniente, et concidentur quomodo in cataclysmo usque ad finem belli, quod concidetur usque ad interitum. Et confirmabit testamentum in multis.

excerpts.citation: Hippolytus — On Christ and Antichrist On Christ and Antichrist (Hippolytus)
excerpts.author: Hippolytus
english: Since you wanted to learn the topics you proposed to us, my dear brother Theophilus, I thought it reasonable — having drawn freely from the holy spring of those divine Scriptures — to set before your eyes the things you were seeking. I did this so that you would not only be gladdened by hearing these things with your ears, but also be instructed by their power and by the realities themselves, and so be able to glorify God in every way. (2 Timothy 1:13-14; 2 Timothy 2:2)

This is to be a safeguard for you in the present life, free of danger, coming from us, so that you may bring forward the things unknown and hard for many to grasp, drawn from ready words. You will sow them in the breadth of your heart as in fertile and pure soil, and through them you will despise those who contradict and speak against the saving word. But I fear these things might be entrusted to unbelieving and blaspheming tongues; the danger is not trivial. Rather, let us entrust them to devout and faithful people who wish to live in a holy and righteous way with reverence. For the blessed apostle did not exhort Timothy in vain when he wrote: "Be mindful, guard the deposit, turning away from profane and empty talk and the contradictions of falsely named knowledge, which some, by professing it, have missed the mark concerning the faith." And again: "You, then, my child, be strengthened in the grace that is in Christ Jesus, and the things you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust these to faithful people who will be able to teach others as well."

And so the blessed apostle handed these things over with caution — things that are not for everyone — foreseeing by the Spirit that "the faith of all will be in danger." How much more will we be in danger if we simply and carelessly hand over the words of God to unholy and unworthy men? For since the blessed prophets became our eyes, foreseeing through faith the mysteries of the Word — mysteries they also served to later generations — they spoke not only of things past, but also proclaimed things present and future, so that a prophet might be shown not only for a time but for all generations, proclaiming the things to come. All of them were perfected by the prophetic Spirit and deemed worthy by the Word itself; they became instruments of themselves, always having the Word as a trigger. Not moved by their own power, they announced the things God willed. The prophets did not speak from their own power, nor did they proclaim what they themselves wanted; rather, first they were taught rightly through the Word, then they were instructed beforehand about the future through visions, and thus sent they spoke the things revealed to them alone by God.

By what logic will a prophet be called a prophet, if not because he foresaw the future by the Spirit? If a prophet spoke about something that had already happened, he would not be a prophet by saying things everyone had seen with their own eyes. But by narrating the future he was rightly judged a prophet. Therefore the prophets were rightly called "seers" from the beginning. From them we also, having been well taught in the things they foretold, declare that we speak not from our own invention. We do not attempt to innovate, but to bring to light the things spoken long ago, whose writings bring them into the light for those able to believe rightly, so that there may be common benefit for both: for the speaker, the ability to set forth the proposed things rightly by holding them in memory; for the hearer, the ability to give heed to what is said. Since a common goal is set before both — for the speaker to speak without danger, for the hearer to receive what is said faithfully — I also urge you, Theophilus, to join me in the struggle of prayer to God.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: Since the pamphlet is being dismantled, I must briefly revisit the arguments that crop up again and simply pass over those that have surfaced repeatedly. I am sick of still contending about the law; I have proved time and again that its concession supplies no argument for a different God in Christ — specifically, the Christ preached and promised to the Creator — especially since this very epistle appears to exclude the law almost entirely. Yet we have also shown repeatedly that the apostle carries God around as judge, and in that judge the avenger and the Creator are one in the avenger.

So here too, when he says, "For I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, Jew and Greek alike, because the justice of God is revealed in it from faith to faith" (Rom 1:16-17), he undoubtedly assigns both gospel and salvation to the just God, not the "good" one — to put it in the heretic's own terms — transferring from the faith of the law to the faith of the gospel, His own law and His own gospel, since he also declares that the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against the impiety and injustice of men who suppress the truth in injustice. Whose wrath? The Creator's, of course. Therefore the truth also belongs to the One whose wrath it is, a wrath slated to be revealed for the vindication of that truth.

He adds: "We know that the judgment of God is according to truth" (Rom 2:2), and he has validated that wrath, from which judgment comes for the truth, and he has confirmed the truth of the same God whose wrath he validated by validating the judgment. It would be a different matter if the Creator in anger were avenging the truth of another God suppressed in injustice. But the ditches Marcion has dug in this epistle — rather, the supreme epistle — by cutting out whatever he pleased, will be exposed by the integrity of our text. It suffices for me that he did not see fit to excise the passages I cite as evidence of his negligence and blindness.

If God judges the hidden things of men — both those who sinned under the law and those who sinned without it — since even the latter, though ignorant of the law, do by nature what the law requires, then that God will judge whose law and nature they are, a nature that serves as a likeness of the law for those who do not know the law. And how will He judge? "According to the gospel, through Christ" (Rom 2:16). Therefore both the gospel and Christ belong to the same God whose law and nature will be vindicated by that God through the gospel and Christ in the judgment spoken of above: "according to truth."

Just as the wrath revealed from heaven can come only from the God of wrath, so this interpretation, cohering with the earlier one in which the Creator's judgment is proclaimed, cannot be transferred to another God who neither judges nor grows angry, but must belong to the One whose judgment and wrath these are, and necessarily also the gospel and Christ, through whom these transactions take place.

That is why he launches an attack on transgressors of the law who teach "do not steal" yet steal — acting as a man of God's law, not as the Creator Himself being touched in these ways, since the One who forbade stealing commanded fraud against the Egyptians for gold and silver, just as other passages are twisted against Him. Clearly the apostle feared to make a public reproach against the God from whom he did not fear to turn away. Yet he pressed the Jews so hard that he inserted a prophetic rebuke: "Because of you the name of God is blasphemed" (Rom 2:24). How perverse, then, that he himself would blaspheme the very One whose blasphemy he denounces in the wicked!

He also prefers circumcision of the heart to circumcision of the flesh. But with God circumcision of the heart, not the flesh, has been effected — by the Spirit, not the letter. If this is the circumcision of Jeremiah — "Circumcise the foreskins of your hearts" (Jer 4:4) — and of Moses — "Circumcise your hardened hearts" (Deut 10:16) — then the Spirit who circumcises the heart belongs to the same God whose letter cuts the flesh, and whose Jew is both the hidden one and the open one, because the apostle would not have named the Jew if he were not serving the God of the Jews.

"Once the law, now the justice of God through the faith of Christ" (Rom 3:21-22). What is this distinction? Did your God serve the Creator's arrangement, giving Him time and His law? Or the One who was then and is now? Whose law, and whose faith of Christ? The distinction is one of arrangements, not of gods. He warns those justified by the faith of Christ to have peace with God (Rom 5:1). With which God? The one whose enemies we never were, or the one whose law and nature we rebelled against? For if peace is offered to the One with whom there was war, we will be justified to Him; and Christ will be His, through whose faith we are justified, to whose peace it belongs that His enemies be subdued.

"The law entered so that the trespass might abound" (Rom 5:20). Why? "So that grace might abound all the more" (Rom 5:20). Whose God's grace, if not the One whose law it also is? Unless the Creator inserted the law to procure an occasion for the grace of another God — and a rival at that, not to say an unknown one — so that just as sin reigned in death, so grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ (Rom 5:21) with His own adversary. For this reason the Creator's law shut up everything under sin and brought the whole world under guilt and stopped every mouth, so that no one might boast through it, so that grace might be preserved for the glory of Christ — not the Creator's Christ, but Marcion's!

I can even establish the substance of Christ here from the prospect of the coming question. For he says: "We have died to the law through the body of Christ" (Rom 7:4). Therefore Christ has a body. One may dispute whether it is a body, not immediately flesh! But whatever its substance, since he calls it a body and subjects it to having risen from the dead, no other body can be understood than one of flesh, in which the law of death is spoken. Yet he also bears witness to the law and excuses its cause: "What then shall we say? That the law is sin? By no means!" (Rom 7:7). I abhor it, Marcion — by no means! — the apostle abominating the accusation against the law: "I would not have known sin except through the law" (Rom 7:7). O supreme praise of the law, that through it sin was not allowed to hide! Therefore it is not the law that deceived, but sin through the occasion of the commandment. What do you impute to God's law, which the apostle dare not impute? And yet he piles on: "The law is holy, and the commandment is just and good" (Rom 7:12). If he venerates the Creator's law in this way, I do not know how he destroys it. Who distinguishes two gods, one just and the other good, when one must believe that the commandment of the one God is both good and just? But if he also confirms the spiritual law, then certainly the prophetic, certainly the figurative. I must therefore establish Christ as having been prefigured in the law, so that He could be recognized by all the Jews.

latin: Quanto opusculum profligatur, breuiter iam retractanda sunt quae rursus occurrunt, quaedam uero et tramittenda, quae saepius occurrerunt. piget de lege adhuc congredi, qui totiens probauerim concessionem eius nullum argumentum praestare diuersi dei in Christo, praedicatam scilicet et repromissam in Christum apud creatorem, quatenus et ipsa (ista) epistola legem plurimum uidetur excludere. sed et iudicem deum ab apostolo circumferri saepe iam ostendimus et in iudice ultorem et creatorem in ultore. itaque et hic, cum dicit: non enim me pudet euangelii; uirtus enim dei est in salutem omni credenti, Iudaeo et Graeco, quia iustitia dei in eo reuelatur ex fide in fidem, sine dubio et euangelium et salutem iusto deo deputat, non bono, — ut ita dixerim secundum haeretici distinctionem — transferenti ex fide legis in fidem euangelii, suae utique legis et sui euangelii, quoniam et iram (dei) dicit reuelari de caelo super impietatem et iniustitiam hominum, qui ueritatem (in) iniustitia detineant. cuius dei ira? utique creatoris. ergo et ueritas eius erit, cuius et ira, quae reuelari habet in ultionem ueritatis. etiam adiciens: scimus autem iudicium dei secundum ueritatem esse et iram ipsam probauit, ex qua uenit iudicium pro ueritate, et ueritatem rursus eiusdem dei confirmauit, cuius iram probauit probando iudicium. aliud est, si ueritatem dei alterius in iniustitia detentam creator iratus ulciscitur. quantas autem foueas in ista uel maxime epistola Marcion fecerit auferendo quae uoluit, de nostri instrumenti integritate parebit. mihi sufficit, quae proinde eradenda non uidit quasi neglegentias et caecitates eius accipere. si enim iudicabit deus occulta hominum, tam eorum qui in lege deliquerunt quam eorum qui sine lege, — quia et hi (etsi) legem ignorant, at natura faciunt quae sunt legis — utique is deus iudicabit, cuius sunt et lex et ipsa natura, quae legis est instar ignorantibus legem. iudicabit autem quomodo? secundum euangelium, inquit, per Christum. ergo et euangelium et Christus illius sunt, cuius et lex et natura, quae per euangelium et Christum uindicabuntur a deo illo iudicio, de quo et supra: secundum ueritatem. ergo qua (ad) defendenda (ea) reueletur de caelo ira non nisi a deo irae, ita et hic sensus, pristino cohaerens, in quo iudicium creatoris edicitur, non potest in alium deum referri, qui nec iudicat nec irascitur, sed in illum, cuius dum haec sunt, iudicium dico et iram, etiam illa ipsius sint necesse est, per quae haec habent transigi, euangelium et Christus. et ideo uehitur in transgressores legis docentes non furari et furantes, ut homo dei legis, non ut creatorem ipsum his modis tangens, qui et furari uetans fraudem mandauerit in Aegyptios auri et argenti, quemadmodum et cetera in illum retorquent. scilicet apostolus uerebatur conuicium deo palam facere, a quo non uerebatur diuertisse. adeo autem Iudaeos incesserat, ut ingesserit propheticam increpationem: propter uos nomen dei blasphematur. quam ergo peruersum, ut ipse blasphemaret eum, cuius blasphemandi causa malos exprobrat! Praefert et circumcisionem cordis praeputi. atenim apud deum legis est facta circumcisio cordis, non carnis, spiritu, non littera. quodsi haec est circumcisio Hieremiae - et circumcidemini praeputia cordis - sicut et Moysei - et circumcidemini duricordiam uestram —, eius erit spiritus circumcidens cor, cuius et littera metens carnem, eius et Iudaeus, qui in occulto, cuius et Iudaeus in aperto, quia nec Iudaeum nominare uellet apostolus non Iudaeorum dei seruum. Tunc lex, nunc iustitia dei per fidem Christi. quae est ista distinctio? seruiuit deus tuus dispositioni creatoris, dans ei tempus et legi eius? an eius tunc, cuius et nunc? eius lex cuius et fides Christi? distinctio dispositionum est, non deorum. Monet iustificatos ex fide Christi. non ex lege, pacem ad deum habere. ad quem? cuius numquam fuimus hostes an cuius legi et naturae rebellauimus? nam si in eum competit pax, cum quo fuit bellum. ei et iustificabimur; et eius erit Christus, ex cuius fide iustificabimur, ad cuius pacem competit redigi hostes eius aliquando. Lex aut em, inquit, subintroiuit, ut abundaret delictum. quare? ut superabundaret, inquit, gratia. cuius dei gratia, si non cuius et lex? nisi si creator ideo legem intercalauit, ut negotium procuraret gratiae dei alterius et quidem aemuli, ne dixerim ignoti, ut, quemadmodum apud ipsum regnauerat peccatum in mortem, ita et gratia regnaret in iustitia in uitam per Iesum Christum (apud) aduersarium ipsius. propter hoc omnia concluserat lex creatoris sub delictum et totum mundum deduxerat in reatum et omne os obstruxerat, ne qui gloriaretur per illam, ut gratia seruaretur in gloriam Christi non creatoris, sed Marcionis ! Possum et hic de substantia Christi praestruere ex prospectu quaestionis subsecuturae. mortuos enim nos inquit legi (per corpus Christi.) ergo corpus Christi est. \'potest corpus contendi, non statim caro! sed et quaecumque substantia sit, cum eius nominat corpus, quem subicit ex mortuis resurrexisse, non potest aliud corpus intellegi quam carnis, in quam lex mortis est dicta. Ecce autem et testimonium perhibet legi et causa delicti eam excusat: quid ergo dicemus? quia lex peccaturn? absit! - eru. besce, Marcion, [absit] abominanti apostolo criminationem legissed ego delictum non scio nisi per legem. o summum ex hoc praeconium legis, per quam (non) licuit delictum latere! non ergo lex seduxit, sed peccatum per praecepti occasionem. quid deo imputas legis quod legi eius apostolus imputare non audet? atquin et adcumulat: lex sancta et praeceptum eius iustum et bonum. si taliter ueneratur legem creatoris, quomodo ipsum destruat nescio. quis discernit duos deos, iustum alium bonum alium, cum is utrumque debeat credi, cuius praeceptum et bonum et iustum est? si autem et spiritalem confirmat legem, utique et propheticam, utique et figuratam. debeo enim et hinc constituere Christum in lege figurate praedicatum, quo et a Iudaeis omnibus potuerit agnosci.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: We are forced to keep repeating certain points so that their internal coherence becomes unmistakable. The apostle presents the Lord as the rewarder of both kinds of merit, and we identify him as either the Creator or — a possibility Marcion rejects — as equal to the Creator. With this Lord it is just to pay back affliction to our afflicters and to grant rest to us who are afflicted, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus coming from heaven with the angels of his power and in a flame of fire. The heretic, however, has erased the flame and the fire so that he would not have to acknowledge our God. Yet the futility of that erasure shines through. When the apostle writes that the Lord will come to execute vengeance, exacting punishment from those who ignore God and who refuse to obey the gospel, he says they will pay the penalty of eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power (Isaiah 2:19, 21). It therefore follows that he will bring the flame of fire — precisely because he comes to punish. So even against Marcion's will, Christ is the God of the Creator who takes vengeance on those who ignore the Lord, that is, the gentiles. For the apostle has set apart those who disobey the gospel, whether they are Christian sinners or Jews. Moreover, to demand punishment from gentiles who perhaps never knew the gospel is not the character of a God who is naturally unknown and revealed nowhere except in the gospel, and not knowable by all. But the Creator is owed natural recognition — by understanding him from his works and then seeking fuller knowledge. Therefore it also belongs to the Creator to punish those who ignore God, whom it is not lawful to ignore. The phrase 'from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power' borrows the words of Isaiah and for the same reason points to the same Lord, who rises to shake the earth. Who is the man of sin, the son of perdition, who must be revealed before the Lord's coming, exalting himself above everything called God and every religion, seating himself in the temple of God and boasting that he is God (2 Thessalonians 2:4)? According to us he is certainly the antichrist, as the old and new prophecies teach, and as the apostle John teaches, who says that antichrists have already come into the world as forerunners of the antichrist spirit, denying that Christ came in the flesh and dissolving Jesus — that is, in the Creator God. But according to Marcion I do not know who he is, for fear that Christ might turn out to be the Creator's. After all, he has not yet come in Marcion's scheme. Whoever he is, I ask: why does he come in all power and signs and lying wonders? Because, the apostle says, they did not receive the love of truth so that they might be saved; and for this reason a working of delusion will be sent to them so that they will believe the lie, so that all who did not believe the truth but consented to iniquity may be judged. Therefore, if the antichrist operates according to the Creator, then God is the Creator who sends him to ensnare in error those who did not believe the truth so that they might be saved; the truth and salvation belong to the same one who avenges those led into error — namely the Creator, to whom zeal itself is fitting, deceiving by error those whom he did not capture by truth. But if he is not the antichrist according to us, then Christ is the Creator's according to Marcion. And what kind of being would he be, that the Creator's Christ submits to avenge his truth? Even if Marcion agrees about the antichrist, I will press the same question: what kind of arrangement is it that Satan, the angel of the Creator, is necessary to him and will be killed by him, exercising the operation of delusion in service to the Creator? In short, if it is indisputable that the angel, the truth, and the salvation are his, and likewise his wrath, his emulation, and his sending of delusions against despisers and mockers — and even against those who ignore him — so that Marcion must now yield ground, conceding that his own God is also zealous — who is more worthy to be angry? I think it is the one who from the beginning of things prepared his nature for recognition by works, benefits, blows, preachings, and witnesses, yet was not recognized; not the one who was produced once by the single instrument of the gospel, and that uncertain, not openly preaching another God. Thus the one to whom vengeance belongs will also possess the material for vengeance — I mean the gospel, the truth, and the salvation. Moreover, to command that the one who wants to eat should work is the discipline of the one who commanded that the ox treading out the grain should have its mouth free.

latin: Cogimur quaedam identidem iterare, ut cohaerentia eis confirmemus. dominum et hic retributorem utriusque meriti dicimus circumferri ab apostolo, aut creatorem aut, quod nolit Marcion, parem creatoris, apud quem iustum sit adflictatoribus nostris rependi adflictationem et nobis, qui adflictemur, requietem in reuelatione domini Iesu uenientis a caelo cum angelis uirtutis suae et in flamma ignis. sed flammam et ignem delendo haereticus extinxit, ne scilicet nostratem deum faceret. lucet tamen uanitas liturae. cum enim ad ultionem uenturum scribat apostolus dominum exigendam de eis, qui deum ignorent et qui non obaudiant euangelio, quos ait poenam luituros exitialem aeternam a facie domini et a gloria ualentiae eius, sequitur, ut flammam ignis inducat, scilicet ueniens ad puniendum. ita et in hoc, nolente Marcione, crematoris dei Christus est, et in illo creatoris [est], quod etiam de ignorantibus dominum ulciscitur, id est de ethnicis. seorsum enim posuit *** euangelio non obaudientes, siue Christianos peccatores siue Iudaeos. porro de ethnicis exigere poenas, qui euangelium forte non norint, non est dei eius, qui naturaliter sit ignotus nec usquam nisi in euangelio sit reuelatus, non omnibus scibilis. creatori autem etiam naturalis agnitio debetur, ex operibus intellegendo et exinde in pleniorem notitiam requirendo. illius est ergo etiam ignorantes deum plectere, quem non liceat ignorari. ipsum quod ait: a facie domini et a gloria ualentiae eius, uerbis usus Esaiae et ex ipsa causa, eundem sapit dominum, consurgentem ut comminuat terram. Quis autem est homo delicti, filius perditionis, quem reuelari prius oportet ante domini aduentum, extollens se super omne quod deus dicitur et omnem religionem, consessurus in templo dei et deum se iactaturus? secundum nos quidem antichristus, ut docent ueteres ac nouae prophetiae, ut Iohannes apostolus, qui iam antichristos dicit processisse in mundum, praecursores antichristi spiritus, negantes Christum in carne uenisse et soluentes Iesum, scilicet in deo creatore; secundum uero Marcionem nescio, ne Christus sit creatoris. nondum (enim) uenit apud illum. quisquis est autem ex duobus, quaero, cur ueniat in omni uirtute et signis et ostentis mendacii. propterea, inquit, quod dilectionem ueritatis non susceperint, ut salui essent; et propter hoc erit eis (in) instinctum fallaciae, ut (credant mendacio, ut) iudicentur omnes, qui non crediderunt ueritati, sed consenserunt iniquitati. igitur si antichristus est secundum creatorem, deus erit creator, qui eum mittit ad impingendos eos in errorem, qui non crediderunt ueritati, ut salui fierent; eiusdem erit ueritas et salus, qui eas summissu erroris ulciscitur, id est creatoris, cui et competit zelus ipse, errore decipere quos ueritate non cepit. si uero non est antiohristus secundum nos, ergo Christus est creatoris secundum Marcionem. et quale erit, ut ad ulciscendam ueritatem suam Christum creatoris summittat? sed et (si) de antichristo consentit, proinde dixerim: quale est, ut illi satanas, angelus creatoris, sit necessarius et occidatur ab eo, habens fallaciae operatione fungi creatori? in summa, si indubitatum est eius esse et angelum et ueritatem et salutem, cuius et ira et aemulatio et fallaciae inmissio aduersus contemptores et desultores, etiam aduersus ignorantes — ut iam et Marcion de gradu cedat, deum quoque suum zeloten concedens —, quis dignius irascetur? puto qui a primordio rerum naturam operibus beneficiis plagis praedicationibus testibus ad agnitionem sui praestruxit nec tamen agnitus est, non qui semel unico euangelii instrumento, et ipso incerto nec palam alium deum praedicante, productus est. ita cui competit uindicta, ei competet materia uindictae, euangelium dico et ueritas et salus. Iubere autem operari eum, qui uelit manducare, eius disciplina est, qui boui trituranti os liberum iussit.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: It was once settled as a matter of who owns the names: they belong to the one who first proclaimed his Christ to humanity and renamed the laws. Therefore it will also be settled as a matter of his impudence, since he claims many will come in his name — a name that is not his, if Christ and Jesus are not the Creator's, to whom the ownership of names belongs. Moreover, he ought to forbid the reception of those whose peer he himself is, so that the one who comes in a foreign name is treated accordingly; if not, it was his responsibility to shield his disciples from the lie of the name, since he possessed the truth of that name through its ownership. In the end, men will come saying, "I am Christ": you will receive them, because you received a similar one; nor does this one come in his own name. So what happens when the Lord of names himself arrives, Christ and Jesus of the Creator? Will you reject him? And how unjust, how unworthy of the best God, that you refuse to receive him coming in his own name, when you welcomed another in that same name! Let us see what signs he imposes on the times: wars, I suppose, and kingdom against kingdom, nation against nation, pestilence, famine, earthquakes, terrors, and portents from heaven — all of which suit a severe and cruel God. Since he adds that these things must also happen, what sort of God does he present? A destroyer or an approver of the Creator? He confirms that the Creator's dispositions ought to be fulfilled — dispositions the best God would have removed rather than established, if they were not his. Yet he predicts these persecutions and sufferings to them as things that will happen, leading certainly to martyrdom and to salvation.

latin: Olim constitit de nominum proprietate, ei illam *, qui prior et Christum suum in homines adnuntiarit et legum transnominarit. constabit itaque et de impudentia eius, qui multos dicat uenturos in nomine ipsius, quod non sit ipsius, si non Christus et Iesus creatoris est, ad quem proprietas nominum pertinet. amplius et prohibeat eos recipi, quorum et ipse par sit, ut qui proinde in nomine uenit alieno: si non, ipsius erat a mendacio nominis praeuenire discipulos, qui per proprietatem nominis possidebat ueritatem eius. uenient denique illi dicentes: ego sum Christus: recipies eos, qui consimilem recepisti; nec hic enim in nomine suo uenit. quid nunc? quando et ipse ueniet nominum dominus, Christus et Iesus creatoris, reicies illum P et quam iniquum, quam iniustum et optimo deo indignum, ut non recipias eum in suo nomine uenientem, qui alium in nomine eius recepisti! Videamus et quae signa temporibus imponat: bella, opinor., et regnum super regnum et gentem super gentem et pestem et fames terraeque motus et formidines et prodigia de caelo, quae omnia seuero et atroci deo congruunt. haec cum adicit etiam oportere fieri, quem se praestat? destructorem an probatorem creatoris? cuius dispositiones confirmat impleri oportere, quas ut optimus tam tristes quam atroces abstulisset potius quam constituisset, si non ipsius fuissent ante haec autem persecutiones eis praedicat et passiones euenturas, in martyrium utique et in salutem.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: The heretic finally drops the Jew—the asp, they call it, the viper—and stops borrowing venom to spit out his own native poison, now vindicating a phantom Christ. Unless, of course, this opinion has other authors too: premature, abortive Marcionites, whom the apostle John branded antichrists for denying Christ came in the flesh—and yet not so they could establish another god’s right, since they’d already been flagged on that score. But because they presumed the incredible—that God became flesh—Marcion the antichrist seized that very presumption for himself, all the more suited to deny Christ’s bodily substance. After all, this Christ never acknowledged God as either the author of flesh or its resuscitator—the best, obviously, and utterly unlike the Creator’s lies and deceptions. So Christ, to avoid lying, to avoid deceiving, and thus perhaps being mistaken for the Creator, was not what he seemed, and what he was, he lied about: flesh not flesh, man not man. Consequently, God, I reckon, was not God either. Why shouldn’t he also have borne a phantom divinity? Am I to trust him on inner substance when he cheated on the outer? How will he be found truthful in secret when exposed as deceptive in public? How, by confusing truth and falsehood, Spirit and flesh, did he deny the fellowship of light—that is, truth—and darkness—that is, falsehood—which the apostle commended (2 Cor 6:14)? Now that the lie about Christ’s flesh is caught, it follows that everything done through his flesh was done in a lie: the encounters, the contacts, the conversations, even the miracles themselves. If by touching someone he freed them from a defect, or was touched by someone, what was done bodily cannot be believed truly done without the truth of the body itself. Nothing solid comes from nothing, nothing full from emptiness: a simulated habit, simulated acts; an imaginary operator, imaginary works. So his passions earn no faith. He didn’t suffer what he didn’t truly suffer; a phantom cannot truly suffer. The whole work of God is therefore overturned. The entire weight and fruit of the Christian name—Christ’s death—is denied, though the apostle insists on it emphatically as truly real, making it the bedrock of the gospel, our salvation, and his own preaching (1 Cor 15:3-4). For ‘I delivered to you first of all that Christ died for our sins, and that he was buried, and that he rose on the third day.’ Furthermore, if his flesh is denied, how is his death affirmed—a passion proper to flesh, through death returning to the earth from which it was taken, according to the law of its author? But with death denied because flesh is denied, the resurrection cannot stand either. For the same reason he did not rise, since he did not die, lacking the substance of flesh whose lot is both death and resurrection. Accordingly, with Christ’s resurrection crippled, ours is also overturned. It will not hold, the very thing Christ came for, if Christ’s does not hold. Just as those who said there is no resurrection of the dead are refuted by the apostle from Christ’s resurrection, so with Christ’s resurrection not standing, the resurrection of the dead is also taken away (1 Cor 15:12-13). And so our faith is empty, and the apostles’ preaching empty (1 Cor 15:14). They are even found to be false witnesses of God, since they testified he raised Christ, whom he did not raise (1 Cor 15:15). And we are still in our sins, and those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished (1 Cor 15:17-18). True, they will rise again—but perhaps as a phantom, just like Christ (1 Cor 15:20).

latin: Desinat nunc haereticus a Iudaeo, aspis, quod aiunt. a uipera, mutuari uenenum, euomat iam hinc proprii ingenii uirus, phantasma uindicans Christum. nisi quod et in ista sententia alios habebit auctores, praecocos et abortiuos quodammodo Marcionitas, quos apostolus Iohannes antichristos pronuntiauit, negantes Christum in carne uenisse, et tamen non. ut alterius dei ius constituerent, quia et de isto notati fuissent. : sed quoniam incredibile praesumpserant deum carnem. quo magis antichristus Marcion sibi eam rapuit praesumptionem. aptior scilicet ad renuendam corporalem substantiam Christi. qui ipsum deum eius nec auctorem carnis induxerat nec resuscitatorem, optimum uidelicet et in isto et diuersissimum a mendaciis et fallaciis creatoris. et ideo Christus eius, ne mentiretur, ne falleret et hoc modo creatoris forsitan deputaretur. non erat quod uidebatur et quod erat mentiebatur: caro nec caro, homo nec homo. proinde deus, opinor, nec deus. cur enim non etiam dei phantasma portauerit? an credam ei de interiore substantia, qui sit de exteriore frustratus? quomodo uerax habebitur in occulto tam fallax repertus in aperto? quomodo antem, in semetipso ueritatem spiritus, fallaciam carnis confundens, negatam ab apostolo lucis, id est ueritatis, et tenebrarum, id est fallaciae, commisit communicationem? iam nunc. cum mendacium deprehenditur Christi caro, sequitur, ut et omnia, quae per carnem Christi gesta sunt, mendacio gesta sint, congressus contactus conuictus ipsae quoque uirtutes. si enim tangendo aliquem liberauit a uitio uel tactus ab aliquo, quod corporaliter actum est non potest uere actum credi sine corporis ipsius ueritate. nihil solidum ab inani, nihil plenum a uacuo perfici licuit, putatiuus habitus, putatiuus actus: imaginarius operator, imaginariae operae. sic nec passiones Christi eius fidem merebuntur. nihil enim passus est qui non uere est passus; uere autem pati phantasma non potuit. euersum est igitur totum dei opus. totum Christiani nominis et pondus et fructus, mors Christi, negatur, quam tam impresse apostolus demandat, utique ueram, summum eam fundamentum euangelii constituens et salutis nostrae et praedicationis suae. tradidi enim. inquit, uobis in primis, quod Christus mortuus sit pro peccatis nostris et quod sepultus sit et quod resurrexerit tertia die. porro, si caro eius negatur, quomodo mors eius adseueratur, quae propria carnis est passio, per mortem reuertentis in terram, de qua est sumpta, secundum legem sui auctoris? negata uero morte. dum caro negatur, nec de resurrectione constabit. eadem enim ratione non resurrexit, qua mortuus non est, non habendo substantiam scilicet carnis, cuius sicut et mors ita et resurrectio est. proinde resurrectione Christi infirmata etiam nostra i subuersa est. nec ea enim ualebit, propter quam Christus I uenit, si Christi non ualebit. nam sicut illi, qui dicebant resurrectionem mortuorum non esse, reuincuntur ab apostolo ex resurrectione Christi, ita resurrectione Christi non consistente aufertur et mortuorum resurrectio. atque ita inanis I est et fides nostra, inanis et praedicatio apostolorum. inue-: niuntur autem etiam falsi testes dei, quod testimonium dixerint. quasi resuscitauerit Christum, quem non resuscitauit. et sumus adhuc in delictis, et qui in Christo dormierunt. perierunt. sane resurrecturi, sed phantasmate forsitan, sicut et Chiistus.I

excerpts.work: On the Resurrection of the Flesh
english: We must now turn to those Scriptures, too, the ones that refuse to allow a resurrection modeled on these 'animals'—let alone spiritual ones—whether that resurrection is presumed right now in the recognition of truth or vindicated immediately at the departure from life. The times of our entire hope are fixed by a sacred stylus, and it is not permitted to set that hope before the Advent, I think, of Christ; our vows sigh for the decline of this age, for the world's transition to the great Day of the Lord, the day of wrath and retribution, the last day, hidden and known to no one except the Father—yet foretold by signs and portents, shakings of the elements, and conflicts of nations (Luke 21:24). I would unfold the prophecies if the Lord Himself had kept silent, except the prophetic voice was the Lord's own; but it is more that He seals them with His own mouth. When the disciples asked when the things that had burst forth at His departure from the Temple would happen, He laid out the order of times: first for the Jews until the destruction of Jerusalem, then for the nations until the conclusion of the age. For after He said, 'And then Jerusalem will be trampled by nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled'—that is, taken away by God and gathered with the remnant of Israel—from there He preaches to the world and the age, according to Joel and Daniel and the whole council of the prophets (Joel and Daniel), of future signs in the sun and moon and stars, the nations' conclusion with amazement; the roar of the sea, and the movement of men growing cold from fear and expectation of what threatens the earth. 'For the powers of the heavens will be shaken,' He says, 'and then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.' When these things begin to happen, you will stand up and lift your heads, because your redemption is drawing near. Yet He said it is drawing near, not that it is already here; and when these things begin, not when they are finished; because when they are finished, then our redemption will be present—the redemption that is said to approach until that moment, raising and stirring minds toward the nearby fruit of hope. Its parable is woven in, too: trees growing tender in the shoot of a blossom, and then the blossom, the forerunner of fruit. 'So also you, when you see all these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.' Therefore, stay awake at all times, so that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things and to stand before the Son of Man—certainly through the resurrection, with all things having been transacted beforehand. So, although it flourishes in the recognition of the sacrament, it blossoms and bears fruit in the representation of the Lord. Who, then, has so untimely and harshly roused the Lord to the right hand of God to shatter the earth—which I think is still intact? Who has already subjected Christ's enemies under His feet, as if faster than the Father, while every popular assembly still cries, 'Christians to the lion'? Who has seen Jesus descending from heaven such as the Apostles saw Him ascending, according to the angels' decree? No hearts have yet fallen to the ground, tribe by tribe, recognizing the One they pierced; no one has yet received Elijah; no one has yet fled the Antichrist; no one has yet wept over Babylon's exit. And is there already one who has risen, unless he is a heretic? He has clearly already come out of the body's tomb, yet still subject to fevers and ulcers; and he has already trampled his enemies, yet still struggling with the powers of the world. And he certainly reigns already, yet still owes Caesar what belongs to Caesar.

latin: Post haec, ad illas etiam Scripturas respiciendum est, quae non sinunt resurrectionem secundum animales istos, ne dixerim spiritales, aut hic jam in veritatis agnitione praesumi, aut ab excessu statim vitae vindicari. Cum enim et tempora totius spei fixa sint sacrosancto stylo, nec liceat eam ante constitui, quam in adventum, opinor, Christi, vota nostra suspirant in saeculi hujus occasum, in transitum mundi quoque ad diem Domini magnum, diem irae et retributionis, diem ultimum, et occultum, nec ulli praeter quam Patri notum, et tamen signis atque portentis, et concussionibus elementorum, et conflictationibus nationum praenotatum. Evolverem prophetias, si Dominus ipse tacuisset: nisi quod et prophetiae vox erant Domini: sed plus est, quod illas suo ore consignat. Interrogatus a discipulis. quando eventura essent, quae interim de templi exitu eruperant, ordinem temporum, primo Judaicorum usque ad excidium Hierusalem, communium, usque ad conclusionem saeculi, dirigit. Nam posteaquam edixit: Et tunc erit Hierusalem conculcatui nationibus, donec adimpleantur tempora nationum, allegendarum scilicet a Deo, et congregandarum cum reliquiis Israelis; inde jam in orbem et in saeculum praedicat, secundum Joelem, et Danielem, et universum concilium prophetarum, futura signa in sole et in luna et in stellis, conclusionem nationum cum stupore; sonitus maris, et motus refrigescentium hominum, prae metu et exspectatione eorum quae immineant orbi terrae. Virtutes enim, inquit, coelorum commovebuntur: et tunc videbunt Filium hominis venientem in nubibus cum plurimo potentatu et gloria. Ubi autem coeperint ista fieri, emergetis, et elevabitis capita vestra, quod redemptio vestra appropinquarit. Et tamen adpropinquare eam dixit, non, adesse jam; et cum coeperint ista fieri, non, cum facta fuerint; quia cum facta fuerint, tunc aderit redemptio nostra, quae eo usque appropinquare dicitur, erigens interim et excitans animos ad proximum jam spei fructum. Cujus etiam parabola subtexitur tenerescentium arborum in caulem floris, et dehinc florem, frugis antecursorem: Ita et vos cum videritis omnia ista fieri, scitote in proximo esse regnum Dei. Vigilate ergo omni in tempore, ut digni habeamini effugere omnia ista, et stetis ante filium hominis: utique per resurrectionem, omnibus ante transactis. Ita, etsi in agnitione sacramenti fruticat, sed in Domini repraesentatione florescit atque frugescit. Quis ergo Dominum tam intempestive, tam acerbe excitavit jam ad dexteram Dei, ad confringendam terram secundum Esaiam, quae puto adhuc integra est? quis inimicos Christi jam subjecit pedibus ejus, secundum David, quasi velocior Patre, omni adhuc popularium coetu clamante, Christianos ad leonem? quis coelo descendentem Jesum talem conspexit, qualem ascendentem Apostoli viderant, secundum angelorum constitutum? Nulla ad hodiernum tribus ad tribum pectora caeciderunt, agnoscentes quem pupugerunt: nemo adhuc excepit Heliam: nemo adhuc fugit antichristum: nemo adhuc Babylonis exitum flevit. Et est jam qui resurrexerit nisi haereticus? Exiit plane jam de corporis sepulcro, etiam nunc febribus et ulceribus obnoxius; et conculcavit jam inimicos, etiam nunc luctari habens cum mundi potentibus. Et utique jam regnat, etiam nunc Caesari quae sunt Caesaris debens.

english: Go learn what times these are from the Thessalonians. We read how you turned from idols to serve the living and true God and to await his Son from heaven — Jesus, whom God raised from the dead (1 Thessalonians 1:9-10). And again: 'What is our hope, our joy, or the crown in which we will glory in the presence of our Lord Jesus at his coming?' (1 Thessalonians 2:19). Also: 'Before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints' (1 Thessalonians 3:13). Paul teaches that their sleep is less to be mourned and simultaneously lays out the times of the resurrection, saying: 'If we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep' (1 Thessalonians 4:14). We tell you this by the Lord's own word: we who are alive, who remain until the coming of our Lord, will not precede those who have fallen asleep (1 Thessalonians 4:15). For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God; the dead in Christ will rise first (1 Thessalonians 4:16); then we who are alive will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we will always be with the Lord (1 Thessalonians 4:17). What voice of the archangel, what trumpet of God has already been heard — unless perhaps in the chambers of heretics? Even if the trumpet of God can be called the evangelical word that would already call them, either they are already bodily dead so that they may rise again, or they have been snatched into the clouds — and how are they still here? Truly most wretched, as the Apostle pronounced, those who have hope only in this life will be excluded while they seize what is promised after it; frustrated concerning the truth, no less than Phygelus and Hermogenes (1 Corinthians 15:19; 2 Timothy 1:15). Therefore the majesty of the Holy Spirit, perceiving such thoughts, suggests in the very Epistle to the Thessalonians: 'But concerning the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need to have anything written to you, for you yourselves know very well that the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night' (1 Thessalonians 5:1-2). 'When they say, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction comes upon them' (1 Thessalonians 5:3). And in the second letter, with fuller concern for them: 'I beg you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him, not to be quickly shaken in mind or alarmed — neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as if from us — to the effect that the day of the Lord is at hand' (2 Thessalonians 2:1-2). 'Let no one deceive you in any way, for that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself against every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God' (2 Thessalonians 2:3-4). 'Do you not remember that when I was still with you I told you these things? And you know what is restraining him now so that he may be revealed in his time. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only he who now restrains will do so until he is taken out of the way' (2 Thessalonians 2:5-7). Who is that but the Roman state? Its apostasy, dispersed into ten kings, will bring in the Antichrist. 'And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of his mouth and bring to nothing by the appearance of his coming. The coming of the lawless one is by the activity of Satan with all power and false signs and wonders, and with all wicked deception for those who are perishing' (2 Thessalonians 2:8-10).

latin: Quae haec tempora, cum Thessalonicensibus disce. Legimus enim: Qualiter conversi sitis ab idolis, ad serviendum vivo et vero Deo, ad exspectandum e coelis Filium ejus, quem suscitavit ex mortuis, Jesum. Et rursus: Quae enim spes nostra, vel gaudium, vel exultationis corona, quam et vos coram Domino nostro Jesu Christo, in adventu ipsius? Item: Coram Deo et Patre nostro, in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi, cum universis sanctis ejus. De quorum dormitione minus moerenda docens, simul et tempora resurrectionis exponit dicens: Si enim credimus quod Jesus mortuus sit, et resurrexerit; sic et Deus eos qui dormierunt, per Jesum adducet cum ipso. Hoc enim dicimus vobis in sermone Domini, quod nos qui vivimus, qui remanemus in adventum Domini nostri, non praeveniemus eos qui dormierunt. Quoniam ipse Dominus in jussu et in voce archangeli et tuba Dei descendet de coelo, et mortui in Christo primi resurgent; deinde nos qui vivimus; qui simul cum illis tollemur in nubibus obviam Christo in aerem, et ita semper cum Domino erimus. Quae vox archangeli, quae tuba Dei audita jam? nisi forte in cubiculis haereticorum. Nam etsi tuba Dei evangelicas sermo dici potest, qui illos jam vocaret; sed aut mortui erunt jam corporaliter, ut resurrexerint; et quomodo vivunt? aut in nubes erepti; et quomodo hic sunt? miserrimi revera, ut Apostolus pronuntiavit, qui in ista tantum vita sperantes habebuntur, excludendi, dum praeripiunt, quod post illam repromittitur; frustrati circa veritatem, non minus quam Phygellus et Hermogenes. Et ideo majestas Spiritus Sancti perspicax ejusmodi sensuum, et in ipsa ad Thessalonicenses Epistola suggerit: De temporibus autem et temporum spatiis, fratres, non est necessitas scribendi vobis: ipsi enim certissime scitis quod dies Domini, quasi fur nocte, ita adveniet. Cum dicent, pax, et tuta sunt omnia, tunc illis repentinus insistet interitus. Et in secunda, pleniore sollicitudine ad eosdem: Obsecro autem vos, fratres, per adventum Domini nostri Jesu Christi, et congregationem nostram ad illum, ne cito commoveamini animo, neque turbemini, neque per spiritum, neque per sermenem, scilicet pseudoprophetarum, neque per epistolam, scilicet pseudapostolorum, ac si per nostram, quasi insistat dies Domini. Ne quis vos seducat ullo modo: quoniam nisi veniat abscessio primo, hujus utique regni, et reveletur delinquentiae homo, id est Antichristus, filius perditionis, qui adversatur et superextollitur in omne quod Deus dicitur, vel religio; uti sedeat in templo Dei, adfirmans Deum se. Nonne meministis, quod cum apud vos essem, haec dicebam vobis? et nunc quid detineat scitis, ad revelandum eum in suo tempore. Jam enim arcanum iniquitatis agitatur; tantum qui nunc tenet, teneat, donec de medio fiat. Quis, nisi romanus status? cujus abscessio in decem reges dispersa Antichristum superducet. Et tunc revelabitur iniquus, quem Dominus Jesus interficiet spiritu oris sui, et evacuabit apparentia sui; cujus est adventus secundum operationem satanae in omni virtute et signis atque portentis mendacii, et in omni seductione injustitiae eis qui pereunt.

english: Scripture also mentions garments so we can allegorize the hope of the flesh. The Apocalypse of John says, "These are the ones who have not defiled their garments with women," meaning virgins and those who made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven (Apocalypse of John). Therefore they will wear white robes — that is, they will share in the clarity of the undefiled flesh. In the Gospel, the wedding garment can be recognized as the sanctity of the flesh.

Isaiah, teaching what fast the Lord has chosen, adds a promise about the reward of goodness: "Then your light shall break forth like the dawn, and your healing shall spring up speedily" (Isaiah 58:8). He is not talking about silk or a cloak; by "garments" he means the flesh. He predicts the rising of the resurrection flesh from the sunset of death. So we have an allegorical defense of the bodily resurrection as well.

When we read, "My people, enter your chambers and shut your doors behind you; hide yourselves for a little while until the wrath has passed" (Isaiah 26:20), those chambers are tombs. In them, those who survive to the end of the age under the final wrath through the power of Antichrist will rest briefly. Why does the prophet use the word "chambers" rather than some generic shelter? Because in chambers flesh is salted and stored for later use, to be taken out at its appointed time. Likewise, bodies anointed with burial spices are sealed in tombs and monuments, waiting to come forth when the Lord commands.

If this is the right reading, what storehouse-refuges could save us from God's wrath? The text itself answers: "until the wrath has passed" — the wrath that will destroy Antichrist. After that wrath, the flesh will emerge from the tomb where it was laid before the wrath fell. Nothing comes out of a storehouse except what was put in; and after Antichrist is eradicated, the resurrection will be set in motion.

latin: Habemus etiam vestimentorum in Scripturis mentionem ad spem carnis allegorizare, quia et Apocalypsis Joannis: Hi sunt, ait, qui vestimenta sua non coinquinaverunt cum mulieribus; virgines scilicet significans, et qui semetipsos castraverunt propter regna coelorum. Itaque in albis erunt vestibus, id est, in claritate innubae carnis. Et in Evangelio, indumentum nuptiale sanctitas carnis agnosci potest. Itaque Esaias docens, quale jejunium elegerit Dominus, cum subjicit de mercede bonitatis: Tunc, inquit, lumen tuum temporaneum erumpet, et vestimenta tua citius orientur: non subsericam utique, nec pallium, sed carnem volens accipi, ortum carnis resurrecturae de mortis occasu praedicavit. Adeo nobis quoque suppetit allegorica defensio corporalis resurrectionis. Nam et cum legimus: Populus meus, introite in cellas promas quantulum, donec ira mea praetereat, sepulcra erunt cellae promae, in quibus paulisper requiescere habebunt, qui in finibus saeculi, sub ultima ira, per Antichristi vim excesserint. Aut cur cellarum promarum potius vocabulo usus est, et non alicujus loci receptorii, nisi quia in cellis promis caro salita et usui reposita servatur, depromenda illinc suo tempore? Proinde enim et corpora medicata condimentis sepulturae, mausoleis et monumentis sequestrantur, processura inde cum jusserit Dominus. Quod cum ita intelligi congruat; et quae enim ab ira Dei cellariorum nos refugia servabunt? hoc ipso quod ait, donec ira praetereat, quae extinguet Antichristum, post iram ostendit processuram carnem de sepulcro, in quo ante iram fuerit illata. Nam et de cellariis non aliud effertur, quam quod infertur; et post Antichristi eradicationem agitabitur resurrectio.

excerpts.citation: Tertullian — A Treatise on the Soul 58
excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: "So all souls end up in the underworld?" you ask. Whether you like it or not, punishments and refreshments are already both there. You have the poor and the rich. Since I deferred something to this section, I will now deliver it at the close. Why shouldn't you think the soul is both punished and comforted in the underworld in the meantime, under the expectation of both judgments, in a kind of usurpation and candid appraisal of it? "Because," you say, "divine judgment must keep its business intact without any pre-tasting of the sentence. Then, too, because the restoration of the flesh must be accomplished, so that it may be a partner in works and rewards" (Matt 5:28). What, then, happens in that time? Shall we sleep? But souls do not sleep even among the living, for sleep belongs to bodies, and death itself is the mirror of sleep. Or do you suppose nothing goes on there, the place to which all humanity is drawn, where all hope is sequestered? Do you think judgment is being weighed, or begun, rushed, or administered? Tell me, how grossly unjust it would be even in the underworld if the guilty still fare well there while the innocent do not yet. What do you want: a postponement after death, with confused hope and uncertain expectation toying with you, or a reckoning of life and an ordination of judgment already dreaded? Does the soul always wait for the body so that it may grieve or rejoice? Does it not suffice for both kinds of suffering from its own resources? How often, with the body unharmed, the soul alone is tormented by bile, anger, disgust, often without even knowing itself! How often, with the body afflicted, the soul seeks a furtive joy for itself and withdraws from the body's importunate company! I would be lying if the soul were not accustomed to glory and rejoice alone even in the torments of the body. Look at the soul of Mucius, when he surrendered his right hand to the flames. Look at the soul of Zeno, when he passed beyond the torments of Dionysius. The bites of wild beasts are ornaments of youth, like the scars of the bear on Cyrus. So much does the soul know how to grieve and rejoice without the flesh even in the underworld, because even in unharmed flesh it grieves if it wishes, and in harmed flesh it rejoices if it wishes. If this is from its own will in life, how much more from the judgment of God after death! But the soul does not share all its works with the ministry of the flesh; for divine censure also pursues solitary thoughts and naked wills: whoever has looked to lust has already committed adultery in his heart (Matt 5:28). Therefore it is most fitting that the soul be punished, even without the flesh, because it committed the offense without the flesh's partnership. So also, on account of pious and benevolent thoughts, in which the flesh did not cooperate, it will be comforted without the flesh. What now, if the soul is prior even in carnal matters, conceiving, arranging, commanding, impelling? And even when unwilling, it still handles beforehand what it will do through the body. Conscience will never come after the deed. So it belongs to this order as well: to weigh the rewards beforehand, which are due to it beforehand. In sum, when we understand that prison which the Gospel depicts to be the underworld, and interpret the final small quadrant — that every minor fault is to be paid there by the delay of the resurrection — no one will doubt that the soul pays something among the dead, with the fullness of the resurrection preserved through the flesh as well. The Paraclete also commended this very frequently, if anyone has accepted his discourses from the recognition of the promised charisms. To every human opinion about the soul, having met the doctrine of faith, we have satisfied just and necessary curiosity. But for enormous and idle curiosity, it will lack learning as much as it pleased to inquire.

latin: «Omnes ergo animae penes inferos?» inquis. Velis ac nolis, et supplicia jam illic, et refrigeria. Habes pauperem et divitem. Et quia distuli nescio quid ad hanc partem, jam opportune in clausula reddam. Cur enim non putes animam, et puniri, et foveri in infernis interim sub expectatione utriusque judicii, in quadam usurpatione et candida ejus? «Quia salvum debet esse, inquis, judicio divino negotium suum, sine ulla praelibatione sententiae. Tum quia et carnis operienda est restitutio, ut consortis operarum atque mercedum.» Quid ergo fiet in tempore isto? dormiemus? Atenim animae nec in viventibus dormiunt: corporum enim est somnus, quorum et ipsa mors cum speculo suo somno. Aut nihil vis agi illic, quo universa humanitas trahitur, quo spes omnis sequestratur? Delibari putas judicium, an incipi? praecipitari, an praeministrari? Jam vero, quam iniquissimum etiam apud inferos, si et nocentibus adhuc illic bene est, et innocentibus nondum? Quid? ampliationem vis esse post mortem, confusa spe et incerta exspectatione ludentem, an vitae recensum jam et ordinationem judicii inhorrentem? Semper autem exspectat anima corpus, ut doleat, aut gaudeat? Nonne et de suo sufficit sibi ad utrumque titulum passionis? Quotiens, illaeso corpore, anima sola torquetur bile, ira, taedio, plerumque nec sibi noto! quotiens item corpore adflicto furtivum sibi anima gaudium exquirit, et a corporis importuna tunc societate secedit! Mentior, si non de ipsis cruciatibus corporis et gloriari et gaudere sola consuevit. Respice ad Mutii animam, cum dexteram suam ignibus solvit. Respice ad Zenonis, cum illam Dionysii tormenta praetereunt. Morsus ferarum ornamenta sunt juventutis, ut in Cyro ursi cicatrices. Adeo novit et apud inferos anima et dolere et gaudere sine carne; quia et in carne illaesa si velit dolet, et laesa si velit gaudet. Hoc si ex arbitrio suo in vita, quanto magis ex judicio Dei post mortem! Sed nec omnia opera cum carnis ministerio anima partitur; nam et solos cogitatus et nudas voluntates censura divina persequitur: Qui viderit ad concupiscendum, jam adulteravit in corde. Ergo propter hoc congruentissimum est animam, licet non exspectata carne, puniri, quod non sociata carne commisit. Sic et ob cogitatus pios et benevolos, in quibus carne non eguit, sine carne recreabitur. Quid nunc, si et in carnalibus prior est, quae concipit, quae disponit, quae mandat, quae impellit? Et, si quando invita, prior tamen tractat, quod per corpus actura est. Nunquam denique conscientia posterior erit facto. Ita huic quoque ordini competit, eam priorem pensare mercedes, cui priori debeantur. In summa, cum carcerem illum, quem Evangelium demonstrat, inferos intelligamus, et novissimum quadrantem modicum quodque delictum mora resurrectionis illic luendum interpretemur; nemo dubitabit animam aliquid pensare penes inferos, salva resurrectionis plenitudine per carnem quoque. Hoc etiam Paracletus frequentissime commendavit, si quis sermones ejus ex agnitione promissorum charismatum admiserit. Ad omnem, ut arbitror, humanam super anima opinionem, ex doctrina fidei congressi, justae dumtaxat ac necessariae curiositati satisfecimus. Enormi autem et otiosae tantum deerit discere, quantum libuerit inquirere.

excerpts.author: Tertullian
english: They know our fasts as unworthy, and some even blame those established for the evening by calling them a novelty, claiming this service, too, must be performed by choice and not extended beyond the ninth hour—according to their own custom, of course. But on the question of prohibition I will answer once and for all. Now, on the specific point of timing: first let them explain where they get this new rule for dismissing fasts. If they appeal to the fact that Peter and his companions are recorded entering the temple for prayer at the ninth hour (Acts 3:1), who will prove they had actually fasted that day, so that the ninth hour could be taken as the fast's conclusion and end? You will more easily find Peter going up to the roof to pray at the sixth hour for the sake of taking food (Acts 10:9), so that the day's sixth hour might be finished by this service, which appeared to conclude after prayer. Moreover, when Luke's own account shows the third hour of prayer, when the Spirit-initiated were taken for drunkards; the sixth, when Peter went up to the roof; and the ninth, when they entered the temple—why do we not understand that, with complete indifference, we may always and everywhere and at every time pray, yet these three hours, as the more notable ones in human affairs—the hours that divide the day, distinguish business, and publicly resound—were therefore also the more solemn for divine prayers? Daniel's practice of praying three times daily supports this: he certainly excepted certain hours, and no others than the notable ones, which became the Apostolic hours of the third, sixth, and ninth (Daniel 6:10). Hence I say Peter observed the ninth hour out of an older custom, having prayed at the third hour with the service of the highest prayer. I say this for those who think they follow Peter's form but do not know it—not that we reject the ninth hour, to which we also observe the fourth day of the week and the sixth extensively; but because we must supply a worthy reason for what is kept by tradition precisely to the degree it lacks Scriptural authority, until it is confirmed or corrected by some heavenly charism. As the Lord says, "If you are ignorant of anything, the Lord will reveal it to you." So, setting aside the Paraclete, the confirmer of all these things and guide into all truth, I ask whether a more unworthy reason is offered for keeping the ninth hour, such that the same reason would have to be assigned to Peter if he indeed fasted then. For the ninth hour derives from the Lord's departure, which ought always to be commemorated without distinction of hours, yet we are more closely bound to it at that hour by the very word 'station': soldiers never forget their oath, and they are more obedient to their posts. Therefore the fast must be kept until that hour when, from the sixth hour onward, the darkened world performed a mournful service with the Lord dead, so that we too may return to joy when the world received its light. If this better suits Christian religion by celebrating Christ's glory, I can equally fix the rule for a late fast from the same sequence: we fast until evening, awaiting the hour of the Lord's burial, when Joseph requested and laid the body in the tomb. It becomes irreligious to refresh the flesh of servants before the Lord's. I have allowed this argument only under provocation—conjecture against conjecture—yet I think I have answered the faithful more faithfully. Let us see if the ancient records also support anything like this. In Exodus, was not Moses' stance against Amalek, persevering in prayer until sunset, a late fast (Exodus 17:11)? Do we think Joshua ate on the day he commanded the very elements to stand still for a fast while fighting the Amorites? The sun stood still at Gibeon and the moon at Aijalon; the sun stood still in mid-heaven and did not hasten to set for a whole day; there was no day like it before or since, so prolonged, that God might hear the man, equal to the sun, persisting so long in the service—a late and longer fast (Joshua 10:12-14). Saul, too, established in battle, explicitly imposed this service: "Cursed is the man who eats bread until evening, until I am avenged on my enemy"; none of his people tasted food, and all the land fasted (1 Samuel 14:24). God gave such authority to that fast's edict that Jonathan, Saul's son, though ignorant of the fast defined until evening, tasted honey and was handed over by lot for the offense, barely escaping death through the people's prayer—guilty of gluttony, though innocent (1 Samuel 14:24). And Daniel, in the first year of King Darius, fasting in sackcloth and ashes while making confession to God, said: "While I was still speaking in prayer, behold, the man I had seen in the vision at the first flew swiftly and touched me at the time of the evening sacrifice" (Daniel 9:3). This is the late fast: fasting until evening, it offers a fuller prayer to God.
